Tutto sulla comunicazione ACI Comunicati Stampa Notizie Riviste ACI Siti del Network ACI ACI Hub ACI Club ACI Sport Sedi e Contatti URP e Assistenza Home/ Servizi/ Pratiche auto/ Agevolazioni IPT: informazioni generali Agevolazioni IPT: informazioni generali Tutte le informazioni utili sulle agevolazioni dell'Imposta Provinciale di Trascrizione (IPT): categorie, veicoli e province Scheda informativa Condividi Copia collegamento Condividi su X Condividi su LinkedIn Stampa Indice dei contenuti Informazioni generali Veicoli con IPT ridotta Veicoli con IPT ridotta stabilita da singole province Veicoli acquisiti per successione ereditaria Casistiche particolari ONLUS - Enti del Terzo settore La provincia autonoma di Bolzano Argomenti correlati Informazioni generali L’IPT (Imposta Provinciale di Trascrizione) è l’imposta dovuta alla provincia per la maggior parte delle richieste presentate al PRA. L’importo base è stabilito con Decreto n. 435 del Ministero delle Finanze del 27 novembre 1998. Si evidenzia che ai fini del calcolo proporzionale dell’Imposta (relativo agli autoveicoli e autovetture oltre i 53 KW nonché agli autobus e trattori stradali oltre 110 kw), gli importi unitari da moltiplicare per il numero dei KW, presenti nella tabella allegata al citato Decreto, vanno arrotondati ai due decimali. Le province possono deliberare di aumentare l’importo stabilito dal Ministero fino ad un massimo del 30%. L’importo totale dell’IPT da versare – risultante dall’applicazione della maggiorazione eventualmente deliberata dalla singola provincia – va arrotondato all’unità di euro per difetto, se la frazione è fino a 49 centesimi, o per eccesso se superiore a 49 centesimi. In caso di ritardato pagamento dell’IPT oltre i termini previsti per legge, bisogna pagare oltre all’importo dell’IPT anche la sanzione per il ritardato pagamento, ordinariamente calcolato al trenta per cento dell’importo dell’IPT dovuta, e gli interessi legali (dovuti sulla sola IPT). Il versamento della sanzione ridotta, per effetto del “ravvedimento operoso”, deve avvenire contestualmente al pagamento dell’IPT e al pagamento degli interessi legali dovuti sul solo importo dell’imposta base (cioè sull’importo IPT senza sanzione). Veicoli con IPT ridotta Leggi statali hanno previsto casi di riduzione dell’IPT. Per usufruire di tali agevolazioni è necessario farne espressa richiesta, indicando sulla nota di presentazione gli estremi di legge ed allegando, se necessario, la documentazione a supporto della richiesta. Alcuni casi di riduzione dell’IPT: Veicoli storici (art. 63 L. 342/00). Veicoli speciali, con la specialità risultante dalla carta di circolazione (es. betoniera, trasporto latte ecc.). L’IPT è ridotta ad un quarto dell’importo dovuto (art. 56, comma 8, D.Lgs. 446/97). Veicoli con IPT ridotta stabilita da singole province Ciascuna provincia può deliberare ulteriori casi di riduzione dell’IPT rispetto alla normativa statale. Alcuni casi di riduzione dell’IPT: atti societari veicoli ecologici Veicoli acquisiti per successione ereditaria La trascrizione dell’accettazione di eredità di un veicolo è soggetta al pagamento dell’IPT. Alcune province hanno deliberato una riduzione dell’imposta dovuta. Le province di Lucca e Arezzo hanno previsto la riduzione al 10% dell’IPT nel caso di trasferimento di proprietà per successione ereditaria. Le province di Aosta, Belluno, Cagliari, Chieti, Foggia, Forlì-Cesena, L’Aquila, Messina, Nuoro, Padova, Parma, Pescara, Piacenza, Pistoia, Ravenna, Reggio Calabria, Rieti, Rimini, Sud Sardegna, Verona e Vicenza hanno deliberato la riduzione dell’IPT sulle formalità trascritte a seguito di successione ereditaria nella misura del 90% per la trascrizione a favore di tutti gli eredi e del 10% per la trascrizione a favore dell’erede che vuole intestarsi il veicolo. Si precisa che per godere delle agevolazioni i due trasferimenti devono essere presentati contemporaneamente e non è prevista riduzione nel caso di accettazione di eredità senza successivo trasferimento a favore di uno degli eredi o in caso di successivo trasferimento ad un soggetto terzo. La Provincia di Foggia ha precisato che per poter accedere alle agevolazioni è necessario che le formalità siano entrambe di propria competenza. La provincia di Frosinone ha previsto la riduzione dell’IPT al 10% per la trascrizione a favore di tutti gli eredi e al 90% per la trascrizione a favore dell’erede che vuole intestarsi il veicolo. Riduzione IPT nella misura del 50% a favore di tutti gli eredi e IPT proporzionale a favore di un soggetto terzo che vuole intestarsi il veicolo. La provincia di Roma ha deciso di applicare la tariffa IPT di cui alla tabella allegata al DM.435/98 (quindi l’IPT senza percentuale di maggiorazione) per la trascrizione a favore di tutti gli eredi e la successiva trascrizione a favore dell’erede che vuole intestarsi il veicolo purché entrambe le formalità siano a favore di soggetti residenti nella provincia di Roma. Si precisa che per godere dell’agevolazione i due trasferimenti di proprietà devono essere presentati contestualmente e non è prevista riduzione nel caso di accettazione di eredità senza successivo trasferimento a favore di uno degli eredi, di successivo trasferimento ad un soggetto terzo, o di rinuncia con atto notarile dell’intera eredità da parte di tutti gli eredi tranne quello che intende intestarsi il veicolo. La Provincia di Firenze ha deliberato di applicare la tariffa IPT di cui alla tabella allegata al DM.435/98 (quindi l’IPT senza percentuale di maggiorazione) per le formalità relative ai casi di successioni ereditarie tra persone fisiche in relazione a ciascuna formalità trascritta (sia per la sola successione ereditaria che, altresì, in caso di accettazione e vendita a favore di eredi per entrambe le formalità), purché siano entrambe di competenza della Città Metropolitana di Firenze e richieste contestualmente. Le agevolazioni previste a favore degli eredi non risultano estensibili ai legatari, in considerazione della differente qualificazione giuridica delle rispettive posizioni e della mancanza di una specifica previsione normativa che consenta tale estensione. La provincia di Teramo ha previsto la riduzione dell’IPT al 10% per la trascrizione a favore di tutti gli eredi e al 90% per la trascrizione a favore dell’erede che vuole intestarsi il veicolo o in misura proporzionale nel caso di trascrizione a favore di un soggetto terzo. Per godere di tali agevolazioni i due trasferimenti devono essere presentati contestualmente. Le province di Agrigento, Asti, Bari, Biella, Campobasso, Caserta, Catania, Como, Cremona, Crotone, Cuneo, Lecco, Lodi, Mantova, Milano, Monza Brianza, Pavia, Perugia, Sassari, Terni, Torino, Trapani, Varese hanno previsto la corresponsione dell’IPT in misura fissa, comprensiva della percentuale di maggiorazione deliberata dalla provincia (vd Calcolo IPT: percentuali di maggiorazione), per le formalità di trasferimento per successione ereditaria. La Provincia di Monza Brianza, inoltre, esclusivamente nel caso di accettazione di eredità con contestuale vendita ad uno degli eredi presentate come formalità consecutive, ha previsto di applicare sull’IPT in misura fissa la riduzione del 90% per la prima trascrizione e del 10% per la seconda trascrizione. Tale ulteriore riduzione non si applica nel caso di accettazione di eredità senza successivo trasferimento a favore di uno degli eredi o in caso di successivo trasferimento ad un soggetto terzo. Cuneo, però, ha previsto che tale agevolazione non può essere riconosciuta ad eredi in linea collaterale. La provincia di Pesaro-Urbino ha previsto che per le formalità consecutive tra privati di acquisto mortis causa e successiva rivendita a uno o più eredi sia dovuta l’IPT in misura fissa. La Regione autonoma Friuli Venezia Giulia ha previsto l’IPT in misura fissa, comprensiva della percentuale di maggiorazione deliberata dalla Provincia (vd Calcolo IPT: percentuali di maggiorazione), per le formalità di trasferimento per successione ereditaria sia nel caso di semplice intestazione a tutti gli eredi, sia nel caso di intestazione a tutti gli eredi e contestuale trasferimento a favore di uno o più eredi in relazione a ciascuna formalità trascritta. La provincia di Trento ha previsto che, in caso di contestuale richiesta di trascrizione al PRA dell’accettazione d’eredità e dell’atto di vendita in favore di uno degli eredi o anche di un terzo, l’IPT è dovuta solamente sull’ultima formalità. La provincia di Piacenza ha previsto il pagamento dell’IPT in misura fissa, comprensiva della percentuale di maggiorazione deliberata dalla provincia, nei casi di trasferimenti di azienda da genitori a figli mortis causa se almeno uno degli eredi prosegue l’esercizio dell’attività di impresa. La provincia di Verbano Cusio Ossola ha previsto l’applicazione dell’IPT in misura fissa per l’accettazione di eredità da parte dell’unico erede che intenda intestarsi il veicolo. In caso di contestuale presentazione della trascrizione a favore di tutti gli eredi e della trascrizione a favore dell’erede che vuole intestarsi il veicolo si applica l’IPT fissa solo sulla prima formalità. In caso , invece di presentazione non contestuale delle formalità in parola, si applica l’IPT fissa per ogni trascrizione. Nel caso di accettazione di eredità e di trascrizione a favore di un soggetto terzo, si applica l’IPT in misura fissa solo sulla prima formalità. Le Province di Ancona, Cosenza, Grosseto e Prato hanno previsto che, in caso di contestuale richiesta di trascrizione al PRA dell’accettazione d’eredità e dell’atto di vendita in favore di uno degli eredi , l’IPT è dovuta solamente sull’ultima formalità. Casistiche particolari Le Amministrazioni provinciali di Perugia e Terni hanno previsto la corresponsione dell’IPT in misura fissa a fronte delle vendite e delle donazioni di veicoli a favore di consanguinei entro il primo grado di parentela. La provincia di Lucca ha deliberato la riduzione al 10% dell’IPT dovuta per le formalità aventi a oggetto veicoli sanitari e ambulanze acquistate dalle Aziende Sanitarie Locali e da altre associazioni di pubblica assistenza (diverse dalle ONLUS), nonché i mezzi di trasporto pubblico acquistati dalle aziende di trasporto pubblico locale. La Regione Autonoma Valle d’Aosta, con Legge regionale n.12 del 24 dicembre 2018, con decorrenza 1 gennaio 2019, ha deliberato che nel caso di cessioni di autocarri o autovetture usate, immatricolati da almeno 5 anni, in relazione a ciascuna formalità di trascrizione o di annotazione, l’IRT è dovuta nella misura FISSA (di cui punto 2 della tabella allegata al D.M. 435/98, comprensiva dell’eventuale percentuale di maggiorazione applicata dalla Regione). La Regione ha specificato che l’agevolazione opera anche in caso di reimmatricolazione (reiscrizione di veicoli usati e di nazionalizzazioni) di autovetture e autocarri immatricolati per la prima volta da almeno 5 anni. L’agevolazione può essere riconosciuta solo a fronte di cessioni. Inoltre, non può essere riconosciuta nel caso di “veicoli di origine sconosciuta”. ONLUS - Enti del Terzo settore Alcune province hanno deliberato riduzioni dell’IPT per l’acquisto di veicoli a favore di ONLUS e Enti del Terzo settore (di cui al D.L. n. 117 del 3 luglio 2017). Informazioni di dettaglio in merito alle agevolazioni IPT deliberate dalle Amministrazioni provinciali possono essere richieste alle Unità Territoriali ACI. Consulta Sedi ACI sul territorio. La provincia autonoma di Bolzano La provincia autonoma di Bolzano ha stabilito che in caso di richieste di trascrizione al P.R.A. di più passaggi di proprietà cd. “consecutivi” (cioè sul medesimo veicolo e nella stessa giornata) l’I.P.T. è dovuta soltanto sull’ultima formalità. Tale esenzione dal pagamento non trova però applicazione per le richieste presentate dopo il sessantesimo giorno dalla sottoscrizione del passaggio di proprietà. Pertanto, qualora la prima o anche più formalità del lotto delle consecutive siano “tardive”, risultano dovute – per ognuna formalità “scaduta” – non solo l’IPT ma anche le sanzioni e gli interessi moratori. rows.title: Import Foreign Cars into India: Procedures and Guidelines
rows.content: IndiaFilingsStartupRegistrationsTrademarkGSTIncome TaxMCAComplianceConsultationGlobalReferWe're Hiring! 🥳LoginIndiaFilingsLearnHR ServicesCar Import - Procedure GuideIndiaFilingsExpertPublished on: Jul 30, 2026Import of Foreign Cars into India - Procedure and GuidelinesA new imported vehicle according to Government regulations mean a vehicle that:- Has not been manufactured/assembled in India; and Has not been sold, leased or loaned prior to importation into India; or Has not been registered for use in any country according to the laws of that country, prior to importation into India. In this article we look at the procedure and conditions for import of foreign cars in to India.Conditions for Import of Foreign Cars in to IndiaThe import of new vehicles shall be subject to the following conditions. The new vehicle should: Have a speedometer indicating the speed in Kilometers per hour; Have right hand steering, and controls (applicable on vehicles other than two and three wheelers); Have photometry of the headlamps to suit “keep-left” traffic’; and Be imported from the country of manufacture. The country of manufacture will also mean a Single Market like the European Union (EU).” In addition to the conditions, the foreign car should also conform to the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the rules made thereunder, as applicable, on the date of import.Procedure for Import of Foreign CarWhoever being an importer or dealer in motor vehicles who imports or offers to import a new vehicle into India should at the time of importation, have valid certificate of compliance as per the provisions of rule 126 of Central Motor Vehicle Rules(CMVR), 1989, for the vehicle model being imported, issued by any of the testing agencies. Also, the importer or dealer would be responsible for all the provisions assigned to the manufacturer as per Rules 122 & 138 of CMVR, 1989 and for issuing Form 22, as per provisions of CMVR, 1989; Finally, the importer or dealer must give an undertaking in writing that the proof of compliance to conformity of production as per rule 126A of CMVR shall be submitted within six months of the imports. In case of failure to do so, no further import of new vehicle of that model shall be allowed thereafter.Ports Allowed to Import Foreign CarsImport of new vehicles is permitted only through the following Customs port at Nhava Sheva, Kolkata, Chennai and Chennai Airport, Cochin, ICD-Tughlakabad and Delhi Air Cargo, Mumbai Port and Mumbai Air Cargo Complex, ICD Talegaon Pune, ICD Faridabad, Ennore port, Kattupalli Port and APM Terminals, Pipavav Port. In addition, import of new motorcycles is also permitted through LCS Benapole / Petrapole and LCS Agartala.In case you require an IE Code or GST registration for import or export, contact an IndiaFilings AdvisorBack to LearnRelated GuidesUnderstanding the Importance of ESI Return FilingsMaintain Payroll & Tax Compliance Seamlessly with IndiaFilings.comIntroduction to the EPFO New Scheme for EmployeesMastering PF Registration: A Comprehensive GuidePayroll Compliance in India Explained: A Complete GuideUnderstanding the HR Services: A Comprehensive GuideUnderstanding PF Return Filing: A Comprehensive GuideFrequently Asked QuestionsCommon questions about Import Foreign Cars into India: Procedures and Guidelines.What are the conditions for importing a foreign car into India?The conditions for importing a foreign car into India include having a speedometer indicating speed in kilometers per hour, right-hand steering and controls (except for two and three-wheelers), headlamp photometry suitable for "keep-left" traffic, and the vehicle must be imported directly from the country of manufacture or a single market like the European Union (EU). Additionally, the car must conform to the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the rules made thereunder.What is the procedure for importing a foreign car into India?The procedure for importing a foreign car into India requires the importer or dealer to have a valid certificate of compliance as per rule 126 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR), 1989, for the vehicle model being imported, issued by any of the testing agencies. The importer or dealer is also responsible for all provisions assigned to the manufacturer as per Rules 122 & 138 of CMVR, 1989, and for issuing Form 22. They must also provide an undertaking that the proof of compliance to conformity of production as per rule 126A of CMVR shall be submitted within six months of the import.What are the ports allowed for importing foreign cars into India?Import of new vehicles is permitted only through the following Customs ports: Nhava Sheva, Kolkata, Chennai and Chennai Airport, Cochin, ICD-Tughlakabad and Delhi Air Cargo, Mumbai Port and Mumbai Air Cargo Complex, ICD Talegaon Pune, ICD Faridabad, Ennore port, Kattupalli Port and APM Terminals, Pipavav Port. Additionally, import of new motorcycles is also permitted through LCS Benapole/Petrapole and LCS Agartala.What is the definition of a new imported vehicle according to Government regulations?According to Government regulations, a new imported vehicle is a vehicle that has not been manufactured/assembled in India, has not been sold, leased or loaned prior to importation into India, and has not been registered for use in any country according to the laws of that country, prior to importation into India.Is a certificate of compliance required for importing a foreign car into India?Yes, a valid certificate of compliance as per the provisions of rule 126 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR), 1989, for the vehicle model being imported, issued by any of the testing agencies, is required at the time of importation.What responsibilities does an importer or dealer have when importing a foreign car into India?An importer or dealer importing a foreign car into India is responsible for having a valid certificate of compliance, adhering to all provisions assigned to the manufacturer as per Rules 122 & 138 of CMVR, 1989, issuing Form 22 as per CMVR, 1989, and providing an undertaking for submitting proof of compliance to conformity of production within six months of import.Can a foreign car be imported into India from any country?No, a foreign car can only be imported into India from the country of manufacture or a single market like the European Union (EU).Do imported foreign cars need to meet specific requirements for speedometers and steering?Yes, imported foreign cars must have a speedometer indicating speed in kilometers per hour, right-hand steering and controls (except for two and three-wheelers), and headlamp photometry suitable for "keep-left" traffic.Is there a time limit for submitting proof of compliance to conformity of production for imported foreign cars?Yes, the importer or dealer must provide an undertaking that the proof of compliance to conformity of production as per rule 126A of CMVR shall be submitted within six months of the import. Failure to do so will result in no further import of that vehicle model being allowed thereafter.Are there any exceptions to the ports allowed for importing foreign cars into India?Yes, in addition to the listed Customs ports, import of new motorcycles is also permitted through LCS Benapole/Petrapole and LCS Agartala.India's Largest Digital Corporate Services Provider & Compliance Platform.IndiaFilingsAbout IndiaFilingsLearning CenterContact UsFounder's GuidePlatformsBusiness SearchFilings.AE for UAEDeveloper ResourcesUsageTerms & ConditionsPrivacy PolicyRefund PolicyLegalConfidentiality PolicyDisclaimer PolicyIndiaFilings Review© 2026 IndiaFilings. rows.title: Il Club ACI - Importing a vehicle
rows.content: ACI Portal Home Cerca nel sito Home L'ACI Il Club Servizi URP Accedi Attenzione: dal 19 dicembre 2024 questo sito non sarà più aggiornato fino alla sua progressiva dismissione. Clicca qui per accedere ai nuovi portali tematici di ACI. Servizi e vantaggi Sconti per i soci - Show your Card! Soci in viaggio Sport Sei in Home / Il Club / Soci in viaggio / Services for EU and non-EU citizens / Services for EU and non-EU citizens / Importing a vehicle Importing a vehicle Importing a vehicle (New vehicles coming from foreign countries or vehicles previously registered abroad) Vehicles coming from non-EU countries First of all it is necessary to register the vehicle with the Provincial Motorization Office. Once the registration certificate has been obtained, the vehicle can be registered with the Public Register of Motor Vehicles (PRA) by submitting the following documents: Ownership certificate If the applicant is already the owner and this is shown in the foreign registration certificate - declaration of ownership with authenticated signature If the applicant is someone other than the registered owner mentioned in the foreign registration certificate - deed of sale with signature authenticated by a notary or public deed or sentence Personal identity document: if this document is in a foreign language an Italian translation must be attached (unless an exemption is applicable under international laws or agreements), certified as being a true and faithful rendition of the original document by the competent diplomatic or consular representative, or by an official translator Residence certificate of the applicant - unless residence is already indicated in the identity document NP2B form for registration with the PRA, available at ACI-PRA offices, the provincial offices of Civil Motorization (UMC) and on the website http://www.aci.it/index.php?id=2160. The purchaser's tax code must be indicated in the form Photocopy of the registration certificate issued in Italy. Vehicles coming from EU countries Documents to be presented if the vehicle is new (never registered before): A photocopy of the purchaser's identity document. If this document is in a foreign language an Italian translation must be attached (unless an exemption is applicable under international laws or agreements), certified as being a true and faithful rendition of the original document by the competent diplomatic or consular representative, or by an official translator. Residence certificate of the purchaser or "declaration in lieu of certification" if residence is not indicated in the identity document, even if the purchaser is an Italian citizen residing abroad and registered with AIRE. Citizens of the European Union (EU) can also submit a photocopy of the certificate issued by the Municipality proving that they have applied for residence, or a photocopy of the certificate of permanent residence issued by the Municipality in which they reside. NP2B form for registration with the PRA, available at ACI-PRA offices, the provincial offices of Civil Motorization (UMC) and on the website http://www.aci.it/index.php?id=2160. The purchaser's tax code must be indicated in the form. "Istanza dell'acquirente" (purchaser's application form) or deed of sale or public deed or sentence. The deed of sale must bear the seller's signature authenticated by a notary and revenue stamps. Declaration of conformity or European Certificate of Conformity with Italian type approval or European Certificate of Conformity accompanied by a "dichiarazione di immatricolazione" (statement of registration) issued by the manufacturer. TT 2119 application form signed by the purchaser, available at the provincial offices of Civil Motorization (UMC). If the purchaser is a legal entity (company, body, association, etc.): Certificate of the Chamber of Commerce with revenue stamps or replacement declaration made by the legal representative to certify the registered office of the legal entity. If the purchaser is a non-EU citizen that is resident in Italy: a copy of a valid residence permit, or a copy of an expired residence permit including copy of the postal receipt of the application for renewal; or a photocopy of the identity document and photocopy of the receipt certifying application for the first issue of the residence permit; or a copy of the EC residence permits for long-term residents. If the purchaser is a non-EU citizen relative of a European Union citizen who is resident in Italy: a copy of the "residence permit for relatives of a European Union citizen" or a copy of the "permanent residence permit for relatives of European citizens". A request note for updating the registration certificate. Documents to be presented if the vehicle is used: A photocopy of the purchaser's identity document. If this document is in a foreign language an Italian translation must be attached (unless an exemption is applicable under international laws or agreements), certified as being a true and faithful rendition of the original document by the competent diplomatic or consular representative, or by an official translator. Residence certificate of the purchaser or "declaration in lieu of certification" if residence is not indicated in the identity document, even if the purchaser is an Italian citizen resident abroad and registered with AIRE. Citizens of the European Union (EU) can also submit a photocopy of the certificate issued by the Municipality proving that they have applied for residence, or a photocopy of the certificate of permanent residence issued by the Municipality in which they reside. NP2B form for registration with the PRA, available at ACI-PRA offices, at the provincial offices of Civil Motorization (UMC) and on the website http://www.aci.it/index.php?id=2160. The purchaser's tax code must be indicated in the form. "Istanza dell'acquirente" (purchaser's application form) or deed of sale or public deed or sentence. The deed of sale must bear the seller's signature authenticated by a notary and revenue stamps. If the applicant is already the owner abroad and this is indicated in the foreign registration certificate, a declaration of ownership can be submitted with the signature authenticated by a notary or by a Municipality or by a Motorist's Telematic Counter (STA). Foreign Registration certificate and a photocopy of the same. TT 2119 application form signed by the purchaser, available at the provincial offices of Civil Motorization (UMC). If the purchaser is a legal entity (company, body, association, etc.): Certificate of the Chamber of Commerce with revenue stamps or replacement declaration made by the legal representative to certify the registered office of the legal entity. If the purchaser is a non-EU citizen who is resident in Italy: a copy of a valid residence permit, or a copy of an expired residence permit including copy of the postal receipt of the application for renewal; or a photocopy of the identity document and photocopy of the receipt certifying application for the first issue of the residence permit; or a copy of the EC residence permit for long-term residents. If the purchaser is a non-EU citizen relative of a European Union citizen who is resident in Italy: a copy of the "residence permit for relatives of a European Union citizen" or a copy of the "permanent residence permit for relatives of European citizens". For used vehicles coming from Germany and registered in Germany up to 31.5.2004 the original ownership document (Fahrzeugbrief) must be submitted. For used vehicles coming from Germany and registered in Germany as from 1.06.2004 a copy of the Fahrzeugbrief or a copy of the new ownership document (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II) must be submitted. Close Menu About usItaly & USAConsular and Visa ServicesNewsroom Search on site Search on site Home>Consular and Visa Services>Services for the Italian citizen>Register of Italians living abroad (AIRE)>Import of household effects Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on WhatsApp Share Share on Social Network Import of household effects Exemption from import fees on household effects is guaranteed to Citizens registered in AIRE who move their permanent residency back to Italy after residing continuously and permanently abroad for 12 or more months. According to recent regulations – art. 15 comma 1 Legge 12 novembre 2011, n. 183 that has partially replaced the previous D.P.R. 455 28 dicembre 2000 –the change of one’s residency back to Italy can be proved by a self-produced declaration, in accordance with art. 45, 46 and 47 of the aforementioned D.P.R. 455/2000. This declaration, along with a valid ID copy, can be presented directly to the Custom’s Authorities in Italy, without any additional consular stamp. At the bottom of the page, you can download the regulation on duty-free imports and a fac-simile of the self-declaration (also for vehicles). This form, once filled out, can be presented to Customs Office in Italy. Should you need any additional information, please contact Agenzia delle Dogane or Customs Offices of the country where your household effects will be imported. rows.title: 9601  Customs Clearance Procedures for Persons Living Abroad (Customs Procedure Agent) (FAQ) : Japan Customs
rows.content: Skip to Content Menu Home Passenger Export / Import Enforcement Trade Statistics Customs Answer(FAQ) Regional Customs Hakodate Tokyo Yokohama Nagoya Osaka Kobe Moji Nagasaki Okinawa Site Map Japanese Site Map Japanese Location: Home > Export/Import > Customs Answer(FAQ) > 9601 Customs Clearance Procedures for Persons Living Abroad (Customs Procedure Agent) (FAQ) tweet 9601 Customs Clearance Procedures for Persons Living Abroad (Customs Procedure Agent) (FAQ) [ For printing (PDF format) ] When any person living abroad needs to proceed customs procedure(*1) such as import declarations and other customs related matters including receipt of notice from Japan Customs, the person living abroad shall designate a person in Japan as a Customs Procedure Agent and notify it in advance to the customs office where the customs procedure is to be carried out. *1: A Customs Procedure Agent who is not a licensed customs broker is not permitted to engage, as a business, in customs brokerage services such as filing import declarations. In such cases, the non-resident importer or the Customs Procedure Agent is required to engage a licensed customs broker to carry out customs clearance procedures. Alternatively, the Customs Procedure Agent may obtain a customs brokerage license. In this case, Customs Procedure Agent will carry out the customs procedures such as export/import declaration, on-site witness of customs inspections, procedure of customs duties payment, receiving and sending documents between customs and non-resident and tax refund from the customs office, on behalf of the person who does not live in Japan. Customs Procedure Agent must have an address or residence in Japan (head office or principal office in the case of a corporation). Notification of Customs Procedure Agent must be made by submitting the two copies of the notification form (Customs Form C No.7500). Please find the guidelines (Japanese only) for you reference. The following supporting documents must be required when filing notification forms.A. Proxy (or documents that clarify details of the contract if you have a contract of proxy)B. Documents confirming the existence of the notifier (overseas register or certificate of residence)C. Documents confirming the existence of Customs Procedure Agent (certificate of all historical matters)D. Commercial or transaction flow chart*Please note that you may be asked to submit additional documents as necessary. (ex. Seller Information (for notifications concerning listings on an e-commerce platform)) For Customs Procedure Agent which have already submitted to Japan Customs until September 30th in 2023, you do not need to submit the notification form again with the amendment of the Customs Procedure Agent System. If there are any changes to the information stated in the filed Notification on the appointment of the Customs Procedure Agent, please submit two copies (the original and one copy for issuance) of a Notification of Change (using Form C7500) to the Customs Office where the initial notification was filed. When you cancel the Customs Procedure Agent you have notified, please submit the two copies of the cancellation form (Customs Form C No. 7510) to customs office where you have submitted the notification of the Customs Procedure Agent. Upon submission of the notifications, you can use NACCS (code: HYS) to file “GT7: Notification of Appointment of Customs Procedure Agent (Notification of Appointment of agent for tax payment)” and “GT8: Notification of cancellation of Customs Procedure Agent (Notification of cancellation of agent for tax payment).” Please click here for the details on the amendment of the Customs Procedure Agent that enforced from October 1st in 2023.https://www.customs.go.jp/shiryo/leaflet_jimukanrinin_e.pdf (Article 95 of the Customs Act, Article 84 and 85 of the Order for Enforcement of the Customs Act, Article 11-2 of the Regulation for Enforcement of the Customs Act, Article 95-1, 95-2 and 95-13 of the General Notification of the Customs Act, Article 2 and 3 of the Law of Customs Brokerage) For consultations on customs procedures, please contact the nearest Customs Counselor.Please see No. 9301 for inquiries. tweet Top of Page Top of Page Notice Privacy Policy Inquiry Customs and Tariff Bureau, 3-1-1 Kasumigaseki, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-8940, JAPAN Copyright(C) Ministry of Finance Japan

rows.title: Motor Vehicle Inspection
rows.content: Inspection Procedure: To undergo an inspection, various documents must be submitted along with the presentation of the motor vehicle itself. In the case of initial inspection for a motor vehicle requiring registration, inspection is conducted at the time of initial registration. In the case of the motor vehicles designated by type, presentation of the motor vehicle itself is exempted upon presentation of the completion inspection certificate. In the case of renewal inspection, presentation of the following documents is required: Documents required by The Road Vehicles Act Application for renewal inspection (OCR sheet) receipt for the payment of inspection fee Motor vehicle inspection certificate Records of periodical checks, maintenance and repairs Documents required by Other Ordinances Verification of the payment of vehicle weight tax Verification of the payment of vehicle tax (or verification of the payment of mini-sized motor vehicle tax in the case of mini-sized motor vehicles) Verification of the conclution of compulsory Automobile liability insurance A motor vehicle carrying a safety regulation conformity certificate shall be exempted from the presentation of the motor vehicle itself when it has been issued by a designated motor vehicle repair business shop (designated garage) which has maintained and had such a motor vehicle inspected by a qualified motor vehicle inspector.

Find out more International schools in France Search for the best international schools in France; you can find a list of selected schools at the bottom of this page. Use the search filters to select only girls' or boys' schools, prep schools, senior schools or sixth forms; or you can search for schools that offer a particular curriculum, such as the International Baccalaureate, the UK national curriculum, a US-style model or the International Primary Curriculum.A renowned centre of European art, literature and philosophy, France has a highly effective public education system that dates back to Napoleonic times. Today, the national school system is complemented by an innovative and diverse international school sector. There are English-medium international schools in Lyon, Nice, Toulouse, Grenoble and Paris, with the capital offering a large and varied menu of international options, including Iraqi, Japanese, Russian, Polish, German, Spanish, Italian and Swedish schools. Bilingual schooling in French and English is also widely available, especially at primary level. France has 21 IB World Schools, with 19 of these authorised to offer the International Baccalaureate Diploma, and three also teaching the Middle Years Programme and Primary Years Programme. All teach in English and 14 provide bilingual instruction in French and English. The private sector also includes Catholic schools, such as the American-curriculum Marymount International School, Paris, and boarding schools, such as the British-curriculum Mougins School and the International Bilingual School of Provence, which offers IB, French, British and American programmes. Bilingual education in English and French is offered by École Jeannine Manuel’s campuses in Paris and Lille. The through-train, coeducational schools, which are associated with UNESCO, offer the IB Diploma alongside the option internationale du baccalauréat (OIB), a demanding programme that involves study of the humanities in a foreign language on top of the French curriculum. The Lille school takes boarders. Education is compulsory for 11 years from age six to 16 and free at French-medium state schools. After five years at école primaire, children attend collège for four years, followed by three years of lycée. A broad-based curriculum is followed throughout, culminating in the French baccalauréat, a matriculation exam that combines breadth and specialisation. The option internationale du baccalauréat (OIB) is offered to academically able, bilingual students by some state schools. Such schools typically offer language support and foreign student fees are very low. France has more than 65 public universities. If you are looking specifically for International Baccalaureate World Schools in France, you can find selected schools on our sister website: www.ibyb.org. rows.title: The Crossbord team: cross-border tax and payroll specialists
rows.content: Skip to content Services Our Services The Crossbord Solution Tax Briefing Service Danish expat tax scheme (forskerskatteordningen) Year-end Reconciliation Relocation service Cross-border payroll See more … Resources News & Knowledge Universe Latest News & Updates Guides & Resources Themes About Who is Crossbord The Team FAQ Our charity council and giving Career at Crossbord Services Our Services The Crossbord Solution Tax Briefing Service Danish expat tax scheme (forskerskatteordningen) Year-end Reconciliation Relocation service Cross-border payroll See more … Resources News & Knowledge Universe Latest News & Updates Guides & Resources Themes About Who is Crossbord The Team FAQ Our charity council and giving Career at Crossbord Search Contact Meet Team Crossbord The Crossbord team handles the full compliance picture: cross-border payroll, tax analysis, social security coordination, and authority communication. We work with HR Directors, Global Mobility Managers, and CFOs who are accountable for getting this right.While we take our work very seriously, we maintain a lighthearted atmosphere in our team, and you will find that humour is an integral part of our daily interactions.If you are interested in getting to know the people behind the service better, you have come to the right place. Jump to the about us section or click on a picture to go to the person (or dog) in question. About us Delivery André Ahrenkiel Manager a.ahrenkiel@crossbord.dk Anne Lind Senior consultant a.lind@crossbord.dk Jacob Krushave Ass. Partner j.krushave@crossbord.dk Jacob Høfler Manager j.hoefler@crossbord.dk Magnus Vagtborg CEO m.vagtborg@crossbord.dk Mathias Jørgensen Senior specialist m.joergensen@crossbord.dk Mathias Kallehauge Senior consultant m.kallehauge@crossbord.dk Mikkel Frederiksen Tax trainee m.frederiksen@crossbord.dk Nicoline Nielsen Consultant n.nielsen@crossbord.dk Randi Vibæk Specialist manager r.vibaek@crossbord.dk Sofie H. Ottosen Tax trainee s.ottosen@crossbord.dk Operations Agne Vagtborg COO a.vagtborg@crossbord.dk Birthe Østergaard Office angel hello@crossbord.dk Guste Vagtborg Office assistant hello@crossbord.dk Jan Tan Cao Marketing consultant j.cao@crossbord.dk Linda Fuchs Mortensen IT specialist l.mortensen@crossbord.dk Line Jørgensen Marketing & AI lead l.joergensen@crossbord.dk Rain Vagtborg Chief Happiness Officer & very good boy hello@crossbord.dk About us AGNE VAGTBORG Chief operating officer a.vagtborg@crossbord.dk Who are you?I’m Agne Vagtborg, COO at Crossbord. I originally come from Lithuania, which was still part of the USSR when I was born. Some of my colleagues jokingly claim that explains my discipline and efficiency.Besides my background in finance and international business I’m deeply fascinated by human behaviour and how our brains work, especially when it comes to teamwork, motivation, and performance.What do you do at Crossbord?Basically, my role is to make things work. In practice that means connecting strategy, people, and execution so our ideas turn into results.At Crossbord, Magnus generates many of the ideas and strategic directions, and Jacob K. and I work closely together to bring those ideas to life and make sure they translate into real progress for the company and our clients.I believe strong results come from clear expectations, honest conversations, and teams that take pride in doing things properly. Much of my work is about creating the structure and culture that allow exactly that to happen.My colleagues sometimes say I’m the glue that keeps things together, making sure people collaborate well and that nothing stands in the way of helping our team grow and deliver the best possible results for our clients.How did you find your way to Crossbord?Originally, I came to Crossbord to help with project management for about three to six months.That was in 2017…Apparently, they decided it would be risky to let me leave.What do you love most about your job?Building an environment, where talented people pull in the same direction and make each other better, is incredibly rewarding.And there is something very satisfying about seeing a good idea turn into something that actually works in the real world.When do you feel successful at work?When the team is thriving and everyone is playing the same game, that’s when strong results happen.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I’m a serious food enthusiast. I love exploring new cuisines, enjoying great meals, and learning more about wine, which is why I’m part of a women’s wine club.Sport is also a big part of my life. I grew up playing basketball in Lithuania, and today our whole family practices karate together.And despite rumours in the office, I have demonstrated remarkable self-restraint, even in situations involving mysteriously disappearing caviar.Personal philosophy: Strong teams turn good ideas into great results. André Ahrenkiel Manager a.ahrenkiel@crossbord.dk André’s work focuses on the complexity where personal tax and social security overlap across jurisdictions, including cases involving posted workers, dual residency, and cross-border compliance for internationally mobile employees. Who are you?I am an old man trapped in a young body. I live with my spouse and our son, from June 2023, in Sæby. I enjoy spending time with my family and friends, and especially going sailing in our sailboat (a Maxi 1000 if you are curious).What do you do at Crossbord?I am managing our consultancy services. I handle direct communication with regards to consultancy with our clients and am managing the rest of the consulting team.How did you find your way to Crossbord?I got Magnus’ contact details from one of my connections who had a spouse who worked at Crossbord (United Tax Network at that time). She was pregnant so I took a chance and asked Magnus for a cup of coffee, and after an 1,5 hour meeting Magnus suggested that I should come work here. That was in 2019 and I have been here since.What do you love most about your job?First and foremost; the best thing about the personal tax area, compared to corporate tax, is that we get to make a difference for real human beings. Besides that the complexity of personal tax and social security in international environments gives a lot of exiting challenges.When do you feel successful at work?When we solve complex problems to the satisfaction for both individuals, authorities and employers.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?As mentioned I am an old man trapped in a young man’s body. I love listening to classical music (especially Beethoven), and watching old Danish movies. My colleagues will also tell you that I am very bad with references from all sort of modern movies. Anne Lind Senior consultant a.lind@crossbord.dk cross-border payroll processing, income reporting (eIndkomst), and managing the full payroll cycle for internationally mobile employees. More on Anne’s work: payroll reporting and authority coordination in Denmark Who are you?I am family orientated and enjoy spending time with family and friends. I am not an expert, but I enjoy knitting, crocheting and similar creative things. What do you do at Crossbord?I take care of payroll from start to finish – process, reporting, and all in between.How did you find your way to Crossbord?I started in a fixed-term employment as payroll assistant, continuing into as permanent employment, first as payroll consultant and then senior consultant.What do you love most about your job?Giving our customers a good experience with our services.When do you feel successful at work?When I deliver the perfect payroll, or when challenging tasks are finished with success.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I started my work life as a stewardess onboard a ship and have lived more than half of my life in Greenland. Birthe Østergaard Office angel hello@crossbord.dk Bio coming soon! Who are you?What do you do at Crossbord?How did you find your way to Crossbord?What do you love most about your job?When do you feel successful at work?Please tell us a fun or surprising fact about yourself? Guste Vagtborg Office assistant hello@crossbord.dk Bio coming soon! Who are you?What do you do at Crossbord?How did you find your way to Crossbord?What do you love most about your job?When do you feel successful at work?Please tell us a fun or surprising fact about yourself? Jacob Krushave Ass. Partner j.krushave@crossbord.dk Jacob oversees the delivery of cross-border tax advisory and payroll compliance for clients where Denmark is part of the compliance picture. Who are you?I am basically a nostalgic who finds joy in the simple things. That’s why it’s a big part of me to laugh and be happy, and I have a home full of collectibles that remind me of the joys of childhood. For example, Disney and LEGO are a hit!What do you do at Crossbord?I am employed as Director and lead our Delivery Team. I have the overall responsibility of ensuring that our customers receive the high standard of service, they expect.How did you find your way to Crossbord?I started as a Tax Consultant (part-time) while I was still a student. After finishing my studies, I continued at United Tax Network and have been along on the entire journey of becoming Crossbord.What do you love most about your job?Going to work every day is super fun. We laugh out loud daily! Crossbord is characterised by the fact that we succeed in combining complicated tax problems with payroll processing. I am sure that this is the right model for solving projects where employees have tax liability in several countries as part of their work. It makes every single day unique, exciting, and interesting!When do you feel successful at work?I often have successful experiences at work. It is a success when my colleagues have good experiences with our clients, so that our clients succeed with their projects.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?Beauty and the Beast formed the basis of my marriage. We got engaged in ‘Belle’s Castle’ (DisneyWorld, USA) and our first dance was to ‘Beauty and the Beast’. Jacob Høfler Manager j.hoefler@crossbord.dk Jacob’s role spans payroll, consulting, and sales. In practice, that covers payroll processing, consulting on cross-border compliance cases, and supporting clients through onboarding and ongoing advisory. More on Jacob’s work: payroll operations and process optimisation in Denmark Who are you?My free time is spent renovating the house, with my 5 children, and my wonderful wife Lina. And then then some is spent on my hobby business byhøfler, where I keep my accounting skills up to date.What do you do at Crossbord?I am a Senior Consultant / Ass. Sales Manager. But titles are titles. I have a hand in everything from payroll processing to light consulting and sales, but it is also me who makes sure that stuff in the office is hung up and that it is hung up straight and level.How did you find your way to Crossbord?Suddenly one day I got a message from Magnus on LinkedIn, and in less than 2 weeks I was employed in a temporary position for 3 months. Quickly, on the first day, it developed into me being offered 6 months and when they where up, I got a permanent position as a payroll consultant. After a bit more than a year I changed to my current role.What do you love most about your job?First of all, that no day is ever the same. And then being part of a team that takes responsibility for both customers and colleagues. If Magnus had not written, I would never have known that the company existed, but now I could not imagine working anywhere else. At Crossbord, I am challenged every day both with exciting tasks, but also intellectually as I develop professionally and learn new things every single day.When do you feel successful at work?I find that I am successful when I complete my share of the tasks, and have created space to be able to take on new tasks by optimising and planning my time.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?If you count individual courses, I am the office’s most well-educated, and I always win on having the most children among colleagues. Jan Cao Marketing consultant j.cao@crossbord.dk Who are you?I am a low-key man with a wife and two children, living a very simple life. I enjoy watching football and professional wrestling.What do you do at Crossbord?I have a hand in everything related to marketing: website management, content creation, social media, and search engine optimisation (SEO). You name it, I am probably involved.How did you find your way to Crossbord?One of my LinkedIn connections was tagged in a photo with Crossbord CEO Magnus Vagtborg. I became curious about what Crossbord does and noticed areas where I could add value to the company. So, I sent an unsolicited application and got hired.What do you love most about your job?I laugh every day at the office. The banter with my colleagues reflects the flat structure at Crossbord. I also appreciate how management trusts my ability to deliver the required results.When do you feel successful at work?I feel successful when I improve anything that helps Crossbord grow, whether it is related to marketing or something else that my colleagues in the Delivery Team need.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I forgot the ring for my proposal, wedding, and honeymoon. Yet somehow, I am still happily married. At least, I think so. Linda Mortensen IT Specialist l.mortensen@crossbord.dk Who are you?I am an introvert, so I love doing something for myself, for example fishing, gardening and crocheting. I also really enjoy computer games, movies, board games and painting miniatures.What do you do at Crossbord?I am responsible for IT processes and digital optimisations of our company, as well as administrating our backend.How did you find your way to Crossbord?I started as a student employee in Feb 2020, and was employed full-time as an IT Specialist in August 2021.What do you love most about your job?I really enjoy the variety in my job. I get to work with a lot of different systems and solutions, and I find it a nice challenge to find proper ways of implementing the right systems for the right job and get them to communicate well together. It is like a big puzzle, and I love puzzles!I love the flexibility I have, the type of work I do and the colleagues I work with. Nothing gives me more joy than hearing the happy responses from my colleagues as they get their hands on a new solution we deployed, and seeing them figure out first hand how the new system/functionality can help make their work-lives better.When do you feel successful at work?When I feel I have made a difference, and knowing that a solution I (helped) make, has made my colleagues have an easier/ better day..What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I like listening to heavy-, speed- and trash metal, and I rode a motorcycle when I was younger, until I totalled it. Line Jørgensen Marketing & AI Lead l.joergensen@crossbord.dk Who are you?I live in Aalborg with my boyfriend and our daughter. I used to have hobbies and enjoy books, TV shows, and movies, but since our daughter is quite young, most of my free time goes to her.What do you do at Crossbord?I work at the intersection of IT and marketing, which in practice means I cover a lot of ground. On the IT side I support our business processes, including data processing agreements, data security, system infrastructure, and of course automations.On the marketing side I handle MarComm and MarTech. The two disciplines overlap more than people expect, and that overlap is where most of the interesting problems live.I also lead Crossbord’s AI work. That means designing our AI environment, evaluating which tools are worth adopting, and building processes colleagues can actually rely on. Data ethics and AI governance sit at the centre of that work. We handle sensitive cross-border payroll and tax data, and our AI environment is built around one non-negotiable: client data does not go into AI systems. We know that’s not a given right now.How did you find your way to Crossbord?When I moved back to Denmark, I decided to pursue a career in IT and enrolled in an AP in Computer Science. I joined Crossbord as a student helper in IT, and when I graduated I was taken on full time. Since I also have a background in marketing and communication, Magnus thought it made sense to put those skills to good use as well.What do you love most about your job?The team. My work is very fulfilling, but more than anything I love being around my colleagues, especially when Rain, our office dog, pays us a visit. I love how much we laugh each day, and how jokes fly around the office. The management team is focused on team dynamics and everyone’s wellbeing, the company vision is genuinely interesting, and I appreciate how our core services are offered to large international companies while the real end user is their employees.When do you feel successful at work?When I find a good solution or a way to optimise something. I also get a lot out of the conversations I have with colleagues. People here are great at giving constructive feedback, so almost every work conversation ends with some kind of improvement.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I once moved to Hungary on a whim. Magnus Vagtborg Chief executive officer m.vagtborg@crossbord.dk Crossbord’s specialism is the intersection of cross-border tax advisory and payroll execution for companies where Denmark is part of the compliance picture. That focus has been the firm’s identity since Magnus acquired the business in 2014, and it remains the basis on which we take on new clients today. Who are you?My name is Magnus Vagtborg, and I am the CEO and owner of Crossbord.What do you do at Crossbord?As CEO my responsibilities include ensuring that we have a strategy and that we are on the right path of said strategy.How did you find your way to Crossbord?This is a rather long story, but in short, I was originally employed as a student back in 2008 and during the transition in 2014 I was offered to acquire the company and then we changed name to Crossbord.What do you love most about your job?I get to spend time with highly interesting and skilled people both within and outside of Crossbord.When do you feel successful at work?When the team succeeds and in particular, when I can recognize some of my seeds in the makings.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I am a rather proficient guitar player with +100 live shows as one fourth of a Metallica cover band in the bag \m/ Mathias Kallehauge Senior Consultant​ m.kallehauge@crossbord.dk Mathias’ role includes tax compliance cases and supporting clients through the full compliance cycle for internationally mobile employees. More on Mathias’s work: international tax and year-end reporting in Denmark Who are you?I live with my lovely girlfriend in our new apartment in down town Aalborg. I spend a lot of time getting the apartment cosy, and besides juggling numbers at work, I throw around kettlebells at crossfit. I probably talk more about Crossfit than I spend time doing it, but that’s the rule, right?What do you do at Crossbord?I do it all. I am so much invested in the company, that once I accidentally answered the phone by saying “This is Mr. Crossbord”.How did you find your way to Crossbord?I started as a student worker, when I was studying at Aalborg University. You don’t throw gold at the street, so of course they kept me on after I graduated.What do you love most about your job?My colleauges, especially the ones in marketing. Besides that we eat a more than healthy amount of cake, and nobody hates that. It’s also nice helping our clients.When do you feel successful at work?When I don’t get teased by my colleagues or get a cake debt for saying something stupid.What is a fun or surprising fact about yourself?I have a tatoo of a heart with the word “Mum” inside. Mathias Jørgensen Senior Specialist m.joergensen@crossbord.dk M

rows.content: Skip to content Services Our Services The Crossbord Solution Tax Briefing Service Danish expat tax scheme (forskerskatteordningen) Year-end Reconciliation Relocation service Cross-border payroll See more … Resources News & Knowledge Universe Latest News & Updates Guides & Resources Themes About Who is Crossbord The Team FAQ Our charity council and giving Career at Crossbord Services Our Services The Crossbord Solution Tax Briefing Service Danish expat tax scheme (forskerskatteordningen) Year-end Reconciliation Relocation service Cross-border payroll See more … Resources News & Knowledge Universe Latest News & Updates Guides & Resources Themes About Who is Crossbord The Team FAQ Our charity council and giving Career at Crossbord Search Contact Relocation service:comprehensive support foremployees moving from Denmark Crossbord’s Relocation Service offers vital guidance for Danish companies relocating employees overseas, whether for short-term or permanent assignments. Our service ensures that both employers and employees fulfil all legal and tax obligations in Denmark and the host country, simplifying the relocation process from tax registration to ongoing compliance. Mastering Tax and Social Security Obligationsfor Global Employees When an employee relocates abroad, it is crucial to fully understand their tax obligations in both Denmark and the host country. At Crossbord, we provide a thorough analysis of both the employer’s and employee’s responsibilities. This analysis covers: UnderstandingTax Liability in Denmark Even when an employee ceases to be a Danish resident, they may still have certain tax obligations if they maintain significant ties to Denmark. We assess whether the employee remains fully or partially liable for tax in Denmark, taking into account assets, family connections, and other factors. This ensures that all Danish tax obligations are clear and fully managed. Determining Tax Liability in the Host Country In addition to Danish obligations, it is essential to determine the employee’s tax status in the country to which they are relocating. Crossbord works closely with local tax partners in the host country to provide a full analysis of the employee’s tax obligations in their new location. This includes evaluating local tax laws, residency requirements, and any potential double taxation issues. Employer’s Social Security and Payroll Duties For employers, understanding their obligations regarding social security contributions and payroll reporting is vital. In many cases, an employer may still be required to pay social security contributions in Denmark, even after the employee moves abroad. Crossbord ensures that the correct A1 or Certificate of Coverage forms are obtained and filed to ensure proper compliance. Additionally, in cases where there is uncertainty about the employee’s tax residency status, we often assist in submitting a request for a binding ruling from the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT), which provides legal clarity about the employee’s tax obligations to Denmark. Seamless Residency and De-registration Management A critical aspect of any relocation is ensuring that the employee is properly registered or de-registered with the relevant authorities in both Denmark and the host country. Crossbord handles all administrative aspects of this process, except for Borger.dk, where we provide support but the employee is responsible for completing their de-registration. Key areas include: Efficient De-registration from Danish Tax Authorities When an employee ceases residency in Denmark, they must notify the Danish tax authorities to avoid continued taxation as a Danish resident. We handle the submission of the necessary forms, ensuring that the employee is no longer taxed in Denmark unless they retain specific ties, such as property or family in the country. Guidance for De-registration from Borger.dk (CPR System) Employees must update their civil registration status with Borger.dk themselves. Crossbord provides guidance and support throughout this process to ensure the de-registration is handled smoothly, but the employee is responsible for completing the necessary forms. Navigating Double Taxation Agreements with Ease Cross-border relocations often bring the challenge of managing tax liabilities in both Denmark and the host country. Crossbord assists in navigating these complexities by ensuring that double taxation agreements (DTAs) between Denmark and the host country are correctly applied. Our services include: Applying DoubleTaxation Agreements DTAs exist to prevent individuals from being taxed twice on the same income in two different countries. We help employees benefit from these agreements by ensuring that their income is only taxed in the correct jurisdiction. Crossbord also coordinates the necessary documentation, such as tax residency certificates, which may be required to claim relief under a DTA. Securing TaxResidency Forms Employees often need a residency certificate (Bopælsattestation) or similar documents to confirm their tax residency status in the host country. This certificate is crucial for applying the terms of a DTA and avoiding double taxation. Crossbord manages the application and submission of these certificates to ensure compliance with both Danish and international tax laws. Compliance withDanish Tax Treaties Crossbord ensures that employees and employers take full advantage of Denmark’s extensive network of tax treaties, avoiding unnecessary double taxation and securing the benefits of reduced tax rates or exemptions as provided under the relevant DTA. Ensuring Tax Compliance in Both Countries Once the employee has relocated, maintaining ongoing tax compliance in both Denmark and the host country is essential. Crossbord ensures that both the employer and employee continue to meet all their tax obligations, including: Filing Tax Returns in Denmark and the Host Country Even after de-registration from Denmark, the employee may still need to file tax returns depending on their income sources. Crossbord assists in preparing and submitting all necessary filings to the Danish tax authorities, ensuring accurate reporting and that any applicable tax reliefs or exemptions under a DTA are utilised. Comprehensive Employer WageReporting and Payroll Support For employers, ensuring correct payroll processing for relocated employees is critical. Crossbord provides flexible payroll support options: either full outsourcing of payroll to Crossbord or integrating our services into the company’s existing payroll processes. We ensure that Danish tax withholding is correctly applied or exemption from withholding is granted where appropriate, and we monitor all payroll processes to ensure compliance. This reduces the administrative burden on employers while safeguarding against non-compliance and financial penalties. Streamlined Year-End Reporting and Documentation Proper year-end reporting is critical to ensure that both the employee and employer meet all their obligations to the Danish tax authorities. Crossbord assists with: Tax Returnsand End-of-YearFilings Crossbord prepares and submits the employee’s Danish tax returns, ensuring that all income earned in Denmark and abroad is properly reported. This includes applying for any relevant tax reliefs or exemptions, such as exit tax deferrals, which may apply when the employee ceases to be a Danish resident. ObtainingResidencyCertificates In cases where employees need to confirm their residency status for tax purposes, Crossbord assists with obtaining the necessary residency certificates. This is essential to avoid double taxation and claim any applicable tax reliefs under a DTA. Documentation forExit Tax andOther Schemes Employees may be subject to exit tax on their assets when they cease Danish residency or other specific tax schemes as part of the relocation. Crossbord manages the process of applying for deferrals or reductions of this tax, as well as exemptions from pension yield tax (PAL-tax) where applicable. Continuous Expert Support for Smooth Relocations At Crossbord, we recognise that relocating employees often face unforeseen questions or challenges during the relocation process. Our team of experts is always available to provide advice and support throughout the process. Whether it’s assistance with tax returns, social security contributions, or navigating the complexities of a double taxation agreement, we are here to ensure that both the employer and employee remain compliant. Our experts are ready to address any concerns that arise, providing personalised guidance tailored to your specific needs. Why Choose Crossbord for Your Relocation Needs? Relocating employees to another country presents complex tax, legal, and administrative challenges. Crossbord’s Relocation Service ensures that these challenges are managed effectively, helping both employers and employees remain compliant with all relevant regulations. Our service offers: Comprehensive Taxand SocialSecurity Analysis We provide a full analysis of both Danish and foreign tax obligations, working with our international partners to ensure complete compliance in the host country. Expert Managemenof Double TaxationAgreements Crossbord ensures that all necessary residency certificates and tax forms are obtained, allowing employees to benefit from reduced tax rates or exemptions under relevant DTAs. Flexible PayrollSupport forEmployers We offer flexible payroll solutions, either through full outsourcing or as an extension of the employer’s internal payroll processes. We ensure that Danish tax withholding is handled correctly, exemption applications are submitted where appropriate, and all payroll-related obligations are met. OngoingExpertAssistance From the initial analysis to ongoing assistance, Crossbord’s team of experts is available to provide support and ensure that both employers and employees navigate the relocation process successfully. Get in Touch for Expert Relocation If your company is relocating employees abroad, let Crossbord’s Relocation Service ensure full compliance and provide peace of mind throughout the entire process. rows.title: CodeMonkeys: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Software Engineering | Scaling Intelligence Lab at Stanford University
rows.content: Scaling Intelligence Lab Home · Publications · Blogs · Openings · Code CodeMonkeys: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Software Engineering Ryan Ehrlich* Stanford Bradley Brown* University of Oxford Jordan Juravsky* Stanford Ronald Clark University of Oxford Christopher Ré Stanford Azalia Mirhoseini Stanford Preprint, 2025 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2501.14723 CodeMonkeys, a system designed to solve software engineering problems by scaling test time compute. Abstract Scaling test-time compute is a promising axis for improving LLM capabilities. However, test-time compute can be scaled in a variety of ways, and effectively combining different approaches remains an active area of research. Here, we explore this problem in the context of solving real-world GitHub issues from the SWE-bench dataset. Our system (CodeMonkeys) allows models to iteratively edit a codebase by jointly developing and running a testing script alongside their draft edit. We sample many of these multi-turn trajectories for every issue to generate a collection of candidate edits. This approach lets us scale “serial” test-time compute by increasing the number of iterations per trajectory and “parallel” test-time compute by increasing the number of trajectories per problem. With parallel scaling, we can amortize up-front costs across multiple downstream samples, allowing us to identify relevant codebase context using the simple method of letting an LLM read every file. In order to select between candidate edits, we combine voting with model-generated tests with a final multi-turn trajectory dedicated to selection. Overall, CodeMonkeys resolves 57.7% of issues from SWE-bench Verified using a budget of approximately 2300 USD. Our selection method can also be used to combine candidates from different sources. Selecting over an ensemble of edits from existing top SWE-bench submissions obtains a score of 66.2% and outperforms the best member of the ensemble on its own. rows.title: TRACE: Capability-Targeted Agentic Training | Scaling Intelligence Lab at Stanford University
rows.content: Scaling Intelligence Lab Home · Publications · Blogs · Openings · Code TRACE: Capability-Targeted Agentic Training Hangoo Kang* Stanford Tarun Suresh* Jon Saad-Falcon Stanford Azalia Mirhoseini Stanford Preprint, 2026 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2604.05336 TRACE is an end-to-end system for environment-specific agent self-improvement that automatically identifies the specific capabilities the agent lacks in the environment and synthesizes targeted training environments to teach each missing capability. Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed in agentic environments must exercise multiple capabilities across different task instances, where a capability is performing one or more actions in a trajectory that are necessary for successfully solving a subset of tasks in the environment. Many existing approaches either rely on synthetic training data that is not targeted to the model’s actual capability deficits in the target environment or train directly on the target environment, where the model needs to implicitly learn the capabilities across tasks. We introduce TRACE (Turning Recurrent Agent failures into Capability-targeted training Environments), an end-to-end system for environment-specific agent self-improvement. TRACE contrasts successful and failed trajectories to automatically identify lacking capabilities, synthesizes a targeted training environment for each that rewards whether the capability was exercised, and trains a LoRA adapter via RL on each synthetic environment, routing to the relevant adapter at inference. Empirically, TRACE generalizes across different environments, improving over the base agent by +14.1 points on τ2-Bench (customer service) and +7 perfect scores on ToolSandBox (tool use), outperforming the strongest baseline by +7.4 points and +4 perfect scores, respectively. Given the same number of rollouts, TRACE scales more efficiently than baselines, outperforming GRPO and GEPA by +9.2 and +7.4 points on τ2-Bench. rows.title: SPRINT: Enabling Interleaved Planning and Parallelized Execution in Reasoning Models | Scaling Intelligence Lab at Stanford University
rows.content: Scaling Intelligence Lab Home · Publications · Blogs · Openings · Code SPRINT: Enabling Interleaved Planning and Parallelized Execution in Reasoning Models Emil Biju* Stanford University Shayan Talaei* Stanford University Zhemin Huang* Stanford University Mohammadreza Pourreza Google Amin Saberi Stanford University Azalia Mirhoseini Stanford University Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, 2025 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2506.05745 SPRINT enables LRMs to dynamically identify and exploit parallelization opportunities during reasoning, reducing sequential tokens by up to 39% while maintaining performance. Abstract Large reasoning models (LRMs) excel at complex reasoning tasks but typically generate lengthy sequential chains-of-thought, resulting in long inference times before arriving at the final answer. To address this challenge, we introduce SPRINT, a novel post-training and inference-time framework designed to enable LRMs to dynamically identify and exploit opportunities for parallelization during their reasoning process. SPRINT incorporates an innovative data curation pipeline that reorganizes natural language reasoning trajectories into structured rounds of long-horizon planning and parallel execution. By fine-tuning LRMs on a small amount of such curated data, the models learn to dynamically identify independent subtasks within extended reasoning processes and effectively execute them in parallel. Through extensive evaluations, we show that the models fine-tuned with the SPRINT framework match the performance of reasoning models on complex domains such as mathematics while generating up to ~39% fewer sequential tokens on problems requiring more than 8000 output tokens. Finally, we observe consistent results transferred to two out-of-distribution tasks of GPQA and Countdown with up to 45% and 65% reduction in average sequential tokens for longer reasoning trajectories, while achieving the performance of the fine-tuned reasoning model. rows.title: Subtitles.love — Tools, Community, and Connection Around Subtitles
rows.content: Home · Community · Tools · Subtitle Types · About Subtitles.love — Where Subtitle Work Becomes Community Subtitles.love is a long-running reference and community site for people who work with subtitles — translators, captioners, accessibility advocates, video creators, language learners. The reference pages live here. The community lives partly here and partly across the platforms we link to. What Subtitles.love Does This site started as a directory of subtitle tools — formats, classifications, software comparisons, the technical bits that translators and accessibility advocates needed in one place. Over time it became a community. The blog and reference pages still live here. The bigger story now is the network of people who do this work and who found each other through subtitle projects. If you've ever transcribed a video, translated dialogue across languages, added captions for accessibility, or worked on the subtitle layer of a streaming release, you know how niche this work feels until you meet the other people doing it. Subtitles.love is the slow-growing knot of those connections — through tool reviews, through translation comparison threads, through the community channels we link out to. The Reference Material Our reference pages cover the basics that newer subtitle workers come looking for. The type-of-subtitles classification page is the most-cited piece on the site — it walks through closed captions, open captions, SDH, forced narratives, and the format families (SRT, WebVTT, ASS, TTML) without the marketing veneer most software vendors layer on. It's been cited in academic and Wikipedia articles since 2024. The tools page walks through the open and paid software stack people actually use — Subtitle Edit, Aegisub, Rev, Otter, Descript, the commercial workflow tools and the smaller-shop indie tools. Updated whenever the landscape shifts. Community and Connection The unexpected thing about doing subtitle work for a long time is that it becomes social. You meet translators on Discord because you both worked the same anime release; you meet accessibility folks on Mastodon because you're advocating for the same captions standard; you end up on calls with people on the other side of the world about a 30-second clip nobody else cares about. Those connections last. Camzey Chat is one of the online spaces where this kind of niche-work community keeps in touch between projects — readers tell us it's where they trade workflow questions, swap notes on tool updates, and stay in contact with the people they met on a translation crew. This site is what brought a lot of those connections together originally. The community side is where they sustain. The two are different kinds of resources, both useful at different stages. For Newcomers If you're new to subtitle work, start with the classification reference. Then look at tools for the working software you'll actually want. Then come back to the community side when you want to ask other people questions. The work is small but the field is welcoming, and most of us got into it by accident. Subtitles.love · Tools, community, and reference material for people who work with subtitles.

rows.title: CS229: Machine Learning
rows.content: CS229 CS229: Machine Learning Summer 2026 Instructors Jehangir Amjad Anand Avati Course Staff Alisa Levin Haotian Ye Isha Sinha Lucy Shi Michael Zhang Course Description This course provides a broad introduction to machine learning and statistical pattern recognition. Topics include: supervised learning (generative learning, parametric/non-parametric learning, neural networks); unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction); learning theory (bias/variance tradeoffs, practical advice); reinforcement learning and adaptive control. The course will also discuss recent applications of machine learning, such as to robotic control, data mining, autonomous navigation, bioinformatics, speech recognition, and text and web data processing. Course Information Time and Location Instructor Lectures: Tue, Thu 4:30 PM - 6:15 PM NVIDIA Auditorium CA Lectures: Please check the Syllabus page or the course's Canvas calendar for the latest information. Prerequisites: knowledge of basic computer science principles and skills at a level sufficient to write a reasonably non-trivial computer program in Python/NumPy to the equivalency of CS106A or CS106B, familiarity with probability theory to the equivalency of CS 109 or MATH151, and familiarity with multivariable calculus and linear algebra to the equivalency of MATH51 or CS205L. Please see pset0 on Ed. Quick Links All links will require you to be logged into your Stanford email to access. Course documents are only shared with Stanford University affiliates.
