Immigration matters often involve complex legal requirements, strict documentation standards, and changing legislation. Delays, incomplete applications, or missing supporting documents may affect the outcome of an immigration case. Individuals may also face challenges involving visa refusals, residence permit issues, or questions regarding their legal status in Sweden. Early legal advice from an experienced Immigration Lawyer can help identify potential issues before they become significant obstacles. Careful preparation often improves both efficiency and legal certainty throughout the process. Many immigration disputes arise after applications for visas, residence permits, or work permits have been refused or delayed. Clients may also require assistance with appeals, extensions, or cases involving the risk of removal from Sweden. Every immigration matter requires an individual legal assessment based on the client’s circumstances and the applicable legislation. At Advantage Law Firm, our Immigration Attorneys assist clients throughout the entire process, from the initial application to representation in appeals where necessary. Our objective is to provide practical legal solutions while protecting our clients’ rights. Family Residence Permit Obtaining a residence permit based on family ties requires careful preparation and complete documentation. Our lawyers assist clients with residence permit applications based on marriage, registered partnership, cohabitation, or other qualifying family relationships under Swedish migration law. Every application is individually assessed, and the supporting documentation must reflect the applicant’s specific circumstances. We guide clients throughout the application process and explain the legal requirements that apply to each case. Our goal is to maximise the likelihood of a complete and well-prepared application. Family immigration matters may also involve permit renewals, questions regarding continued residence, or appeals following a refusal. Every family situation is unique, requiring legal advice tailored to the individual circumstances of the applicant and their family members. Our Residence Permit Lawyers assist clients in preparing applications, responding to requests from the authorities, and representing them during appeal proceedings where appropriate. We focus on providing clear legal guidance while ensuring compliance with Swedish migration legislation. Our legal support helps clients navigate every stage of the immigration process with confidence. Self-Employed Work Permit Entrepreneurs who wish to establish or operate a business in Sweden must meet the requirements for a work permit in Sweden and, where applicable, a residence permit. Our lawyers assist clients throughout the application process by reviewing eligibility, preparing supporting documentation, and ensuring that applications are complete before submission. Every case is assessed individually based on the applicant’s business activities and personal circumstances. Proper preparation reduces the risk of unnecessary delays or requests for additional information. We provide practical legal guidance throughout every stage of the process. We also assist business owners with permit renewals, changes to existing permits, and legal questions that arise while operating a business in Sweden. Our Work Permit Lawyers advise entrepreneurs on the applicable migration rules and help them understand their legal obligations. Where necessary, we represent clients in communications with the Swedish Migration Agency and in appeal proceedings. Our objective is to help clients build a stable legal foundation for their business activities in Sweden. Every matter is handled with careful attention to the client’s long-term goals. Visa Lawyer for Sweden Applying for a visa to Sweden requires accurate documentation and compliance with Swedish immigration regulations. Our Visa Lawyers assist clients with applications for visitor visas, business travel, and other visa-related matters by ensuring that all required documentation is properly prepared. We also provide legal advice regarding visa extensions and the applicable legal requirements. Every application is carefully reviewed before submission to minimise the risk of unnecessary delays. Our legal support is tailored to each client’s individual circumstances. If a visa application has been refused, our Visa Appeal Lawyers evaluate the decision and advise clients on the available legal remedies. We assist in preparing appeals, gathering supporting evidence, and presenting legal arguments where appropriate. Every appeal is assessed on its own facts and the applicable migration legislation. We work closely with clients throughout the appeal process to ensure that their case is presented as clearly and effectively as possible. Our goal is to protect our clients’ rights while pursuing the strongest available legal solution. Citizenship Attorney Sweden Becoming a Swedish citizen is an important step that requires compliance with the legal requirements established under Swedish nationality legislation. Our Citizenship Lawyers assist clients with Swedish citizenship applications, eligibility assessments, and the preparation of complete application documents. We explain the legal requirements that apply to each case and provide guidance throughout the application process. Every matter is assessed individually based on the applicant’s circumstances. Careful preparation contributes to a stronger application. We also assist clients whose citizenship applications have been delayed or refused by reviewing the decision and advising on the available legal options. Our Citizenship Attorneys prepare appeals where appropriate and represent clients throughout the appeal process. We also advise on questions relating to dual citizenship and other nationality matters under Swedish law. Our focus is to provide clear legal guidance and effective representation throughout every stage of the citizenship process. We work closely with each client to ensure that their application receives careful legal attention. Who Should Hire a Migration Lawyer? An experienced Migration Lawyer can assist anyone facing legal questions under Swedish immigration law. Individuals applying for residence permits, work permits, visas, or Swedish citizenship often benefit from professional legal guidance to ensure that their applications are complete and meet the applicable legal requirements. Families seeking reunification may also require assistance with documentation and the residence permit process. Early legal advice can help reduce delays and minimise the risk of avoidable mistakes. Every immigration matter should be assessed based on the applicant’s individual circumstances. Employers recruiting international employees, entrepreneurs establishing businesses in Sweden, students planning to study, and individuals seeking protection may also require legal support. Our Immigration Lawyers assist clients with applications, permit renewals, appeals, and communication with the Swedish Migration Agency. We also advise third-country nationals on the immigration rules that apply to their specific situations. Whether the matter concerns an initial application or a complex appeal, our legal advice is tailored to each client’s needs. Our objective is to provide practical and effective solutions throughout the immigration process. Legal Matters Handled by Our Immigration Attorney At Advantage Law Firm, our Immigration Attorneys advise clients on a broad range of Swedish immigration matters. We assist with residence permit applications, work permits, visitor visas, family-based immigration, Swedish citizenship applications, and legal issues affecting third-country nationals. We also provide legal advice regarding permit renewals, changes of status, and immigration-related documentation. Every matter is reviewed individually to ensure that the application or legal strategy reflects the client’s circumstances. Our lawyers work proactively to minimise delays and reduce legal risks. We also represent clients in immigration appeals and proceedings before the Swedish Migration Agency and the migration courts where required. Our legal services include preparing applications, reviewing authority decisions, drafting legal submissions, and representing clients throughout the appeal process. Whether you require assistance from a Work Permit Lawyer, Visa Appeal Lawyer or Citizenship Lawyer, we provide comprehensive legal support tailored to your case. We are committed to protecting our clients’ rights while pursuing practical and legally sound solutions. Every case receives personal attention and careful legal analysis. Why Choose Our Swedish Immigration Attorney Extensive Migration Law Experience Our lawyers have extensive experience assisting individuals, families, employers, and entrepreneurs with Swedish immigration matters. Personalised Legal Advice Every immigration case is unique, and we tailor our legal strategy to the client's individual circumstances and objectives. Comprehensive Immigration Services We assist with residence permits, work permits, visas, Swedish citizenship applications, and immigration appeals. Practical and Strategic Guidance Our legal advice combines in-depth knowledge of Swedish migration law with practical solutions designed to reduce legal risks and delays. Inspired by our exceptional teachers, supportive community, and stimulating curriculum, our IBDP students develop the intellectual and interpersonal skills they need to thrive as successful global citizens. Academic ExcellenceIB Diploma ProgrammeTHE IBDP at nais dublinThe International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) is a globally respected two-year university preparation course offered in the final years of secondary school (ages 16 to 18 at our IB school in Dublin). The demanding but rewarding IBDP enables students to grow as global citizens while building the knowledge, confidence, and independence to thrive at university and beyond.The IBDP blends stimulating academics with enriching creative experiences and multicultural exposure. An international qualification recognised by top universities worldwide, the IB Diploma is particularly useful for students who plan to study abroad. THE IBDP: A COMPREHENSIVE EDUCATION WITH PERSONALISED PATHWAYSThe International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) provides a truly holistic education with opportunities to specialise in IBDP subject areas.At NAIS Dublin, our IB curriculum students study six subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, and the Arts. Each student selects three subject groups to take at higher level and three at standard level.In addition, our young people enhance their creativity, critical thinking, and research skills by completing NAIS Dublin’s IBDP core programme.The three elements of the IB core programme:Theory of Knowledge (TOK): a course on critical thinking, exploring how we learn and build knowledge.The Extended Essay: an in-depth independent research project focused on a specific topic.Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS): a range of activities through which students strengthen their creative skills, their health and wellbeing, and their commitment to the community.primary SecondaryA TYPICAL DAY AT NAIS DUBLINWith our dynamic curriculum, world-class teachers, and inspiring learning spaces, no two days are the same at NAIS Dublin.Tutor TimeA focus on wellbeing helps our students prepare for the day ahead. Activities such as mindfulness, movement and a focus on relationship building are part of the PERMAH model of wellbeing which supports positive emotions, engagement, positive relationships, meaningful accomplishment and health. Tutor TimeInquiring EarlyShaping curious, creative and collaborative learners, inquiry based learning sits at the core of our curriculum. Taking a deep dive into a range of issues, student develop an understanding of the world around them.Inquiring EarlyNurturing CreativityShowcasing their unique talents we channel and nurture our students creativity. Our extensive arts programme explores a rich variety of genres in art, music, dance and drama.Nurturing CreativityLet’s Eat and MingleEvery student needs fuel to make the most of their learning! With a range of healthy and delicious meals, prepared by our onsite catering team in our Lunchbox, students get all the nutrition they need to perform at their best, then have time to socialise, play sports and relax before afternoon lessons.Let’s Eat and MingleThink STEAMSecondary students enjoy regular STEAM collaboration days in which they work on challenges set by MIT professors, developing their abilities to innovate, think critically and solve problems. Think STEAMGetting That Bit ExtraThe fun doesn’t stop when the bell rings! Burness Paull’s dedicated team of Immigration lawyers understand the importance of global mobility to businesses and specialise in facilitating international relocations, transfers and global mobility planning. We help organisations attract and retain top talent from across the globe. We provide advice and support to a wide range of businesses who currently employ or are considering employing foreign nationals. We provide advice to investors, entrepreneurs and others seeking to relocate themselves or their businesses to the UK. We have a dedicated and experienced team of Immigration law practitioners who understand the uncertainty, frustrations and rigours associated with UK Immigration law and policy. We have an established reputation for providing pragmatic and innovative solutions. Our experience covers all aspects of business immigration law. We pride ourselves on an in depth technical knowledge covering all UK Immigration law options and on providing exceptional client service. We provide first class representation on all aspects of the immigration journey whether applying from within the UK or abroad. We have extensive experience in Immigration litigation covering cases through the First tier tribunal, Upper Tribunal, Court of Session and the UK Supreme Court. We have been responsible for a number of judgements of national significance resulting in changes in Immigration legislation and rules which demonstrates our ability to meet novel legal challenges with strategic solutions. We have been recognised for our work in Scotland by both Chambers and Legal 500 directories and Who's Who Legal rated as a Tier 1 firm for several years. We are members of the Immigration Law Practitioners’ Association. Why and when should you contact an immigration lawyer? rows.title: Learning & Teaching — International School of Dublin (ISD)
rows.content: 0 Skip to Content Home About Us Admissions Learning & Teaching School Life FAQ Contact Open Menu Close Menu Home About Us Admissions Learning & Teaching School Life FAQ Contact Open Menu Close Menu Home About Us Admissions Learning & Teaching School Life FAQ Contact Learning & TeachingOur Approach at International School of Dublin What is IB I Benefits of IB Education I Primary IB I Class Grouping IPersonal Development I Language Support One of the fundamental goals of an education at the International School of Dublin (ISD) is to encourage a love of learning. Welcoming and lively learning environments are characterised by collaborative and purposeful activity. What is the International Baccalaureate (IB) All teaching and learning at International School of Dublin is guided by the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme (IB PYP). Small class sizes are guided by international experienced teachers who work to facilitate holistic and innovative forms of engagement which promote learning that is process, rather than topic driven. Ultimately, ISD students are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to become autonomous lifelong learners.The International Baccalaureate (IB) is a leading global education programme founded in 1968 in Geneva, Switzerland. It offers a rigorous, inquiry-based curriculum that encourages critical thinking, global awareness, and personal growth. With programmes for students aged 3 to 19, the IB is recognised worldwide for its high academic standards and its mission to develop caring, knowledgeable, and internationally minded young people.At International School of Dublin we currently offer the Primary Years Programme (PYP) for ages 3.5 to 12 years. “Imagine a worldwide community of schools, educators and students with a shared vision and mission to empower young people with the skills, values and knowledge to create a better and more peaceful world. This is the International Baccalaureate”— International Baccalaureate Organisation Benefits of an International Baccalaureate Education The benefits of an IB education reach far and wide across the educational community. Students learn how to learn, are confident inquirers who take their responsibilities as world citizens seriously. IB Students: Learn how to learn and take ownership of their learning processAre encouraged to inquire, ask questions and think independentlyDevelop strong social and emotional characteristics, are internationally minded, respect and appreciate all culturesAre confident communicators who work collaboratively with othersAre responsible citizens who take Action to better the worldAre motivated lifelong autonomous learnersTransition well to different types of schools and curricula IB World Schools: Are subject to strict accreditation and rigorous evaluation processesFollow research-based best teaching practicesProvide internationally recognised standardsMeet or exceed local curricular standardsProvide ongoing professional development to ensure all educators are creative and innovative in practiceCollaborate and provide shared learning experience with the global community and other IB schools IB Graduates Benefit from universities and colleges developing recognition policies making it clear how IB students gain places on their coursesAttend all types of third level education including highest ranking universities around the worldAre highly likely to complete undergraduate degrees and pursue graduate workAre prepared for college level coursework, are able to cope with demanding workloads and are likely to be engaged in various aspects of university lifeProvide ongoing professional development to ensure all educators are creative and innovative in practiceHave an established global network with fellow IB alumni. The Primary IB Programme The Primary Years Programme (PYP) focuses on the education of students aged 3-12 years. It comprises a curriculum that is engaging and relevant across the globe.Students learn in an inquiry based transdisciplinary manner, which means they focus on issues that transfer across the subject areas.The programme is underpinned by six themes selected for their relevance to the real world. The themes are taught across the academic year through Units of Inquiry.PYP themes:Who we areWhere we are in place and timeHow we express ourselvesHow the world worksHow we organise ourselvesSharing the planetThe PYP focuses on the holistic development of a child: academic, social, physical and emotional. Students learn how to think for themselves and take responsibility for their own learning through an inquiry approach. Students acquire the necessary tools to co-construct knowledge. They focus on acquisition as well as the development of skills necessary to lead successful lives.The PYP community is committed to developing the attributes of the IB Learner Profile among its members. As a community of life-long learners and inquirers, every member is expected to take Action to positively impact local and/or global communities. Class Groupings Our aim is to place each child in a stimulating and challenging class that provides the best opportunities to make academic and social progress. Our classes have an impressively low student-teacher ratio of roughly 7:1. At ISD there are four, multi-grade level classes. Below, please see placement dates for each class. In cases where the school, along with parents/guardians, believe a certain placement should be reviewed in the best interest of a child, ISD retains flexibility in relation to class placement. Class Grades & Ages Pre- Kindergarten: Child must be 3.5 years when they begin at ISDKindergarten 1: Child must be 4 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentKindergarten 2: Child must be 5 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentGrade 1: Child must be 6 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentGrade 2 : Child must be 7 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentGrade 3 : Child must be 8 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentGrade 4 : Child must be 9 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentGrade 5 : Child must be 10 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolmentGrade 6 : Child must be 11 years of age by August 31st of year of enrolment Four key components form the basis of an IB education: Inquiry, Student-Centred, Skills for the Future, and Global Contexts. The Four Key IB Components 1. Inquiry The search for meaning is fundamental to what it is to be human. Curiosity, asking questions and making sense of the world activates higher-order thinking on many levels. Inquiry focuses on understanding concepts and making connections that enhance learning.At ISD we strive for our students to be active inquirers, learners who are engaged in educational material and experiences. Throughout the curriculum, students are guided by the inquiry cycle. The nature of a cycle is flexible and never ending, a process of which one may move forward, backward and in all directions. The cycle provides opportunities for students to navigate their learning in a personally significant manner. 2. Student Centered Placing learners at the heart of the learning process shifts the focus and ownership of education from the teacher to student. It provides choice, agency and self-efficacy.A student-centred approach allows learners to retain far more knowledge. At ISD learning begins with reflecting on prior knowledge. Teachers gently guide, encourage and inspire students to build upon what they already know, making connections and developing questions for exploration.Through experiences and interactions, students naturally develop intricate, multi-layered perceptions and understandings. When students are agents of their own learning, they become responsible for and take ownership of the learning processes.“Tell me and I forget. Teach me and I remember. Involve me and I learn.” –Benjamin Franklin 3. Skills for the Future n an ever changing world, the future is unpredictable.We do not know what kind of world our students will grow up in. At ISD, we prepare our learners for the unknown by creating learning experiences with meaningful and authentic contexts.This provides students the opportunities to develop a toolkit of skills to draw upon throughout life. We encourage the development of a well rounded learner with character, someone who:engages and is eager to learnthinks for themselvesis capable of collaborationresponds to real-life situations and challenges with optimismexhibits confidence, responsibility and all traits of the IB Learner Profilecontinually reflectsis internationally-minded 4. Global Contexts The IBPYP curriculum framework is guided by six transdisciplinary themes of global significance.The themes have been created with scope and significance regardless of age and geography and are a commonality amongst IB schools worldwide; allowing learners to understand what it is to be internationally-minded.Internationally-minded students are open to others and to the world; they are cognizant of humans’ deep interconnectedness. They recognise their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet to help create a better a more peaceful world.Learners at ISD regularly connect their learning to engage with local and global opportunities. The school atmosphere fosters the allegiance of its students to their cultural heritage and promotes respect and tolerance between all cultures. All community members are encouraged to consider themselves as global citizens and to reflect on how their personal actions can influence others both locally and globally. Personal Development ISD focuses on a holistic approach to education developing students’ academic, social and emotional wellbeing.Wellbeing is linked to all aspects of a student’s experience at school and beyond. It is paramount for our students to feel empowered by their learning, to value and take responsibility for their learning and to demonstrate resilience.Such learners are able to reflect on themselves, their experiences and the process of learning in order to demonstrate commitment to personal growth.Personal development permeates the entire curriculum and therefore is taught within the contexts of the Units of Inquiry as well as through teaching and learning experiences in other areas.The development of physical, emotional, cognitive, spiritual and social health are important features of the curriculum. In addition, personal development is underpinned by the IB Learner Profile, which describes a broad range of human capacities and responsibilities that go beyond academic success.Understanding one’s identity shapes a person’s self-worth and affects their approach to learning as well as their interactions and attitudes towards others. An understanding of one’s own identity shapes one’s concept of self-worth and affects his or her approach to learning and how he or she interacts with others.An understanding of and appreciation for other cultures shapes international-mindedness. At ISD we nurture independent thinking skills, which aim to help students develop self confidence and passion for learning. Interpersonal relationships are fundamental in all developmental aspects and we emphasise the importance of productive and healthy relationships. Language Support Language plays a key role in human development. We use languages to communicate with others and learn about the world around us. Learning more than one language gives students the opportunity to broaden their horizons.Wellbeing is linked to all aspects of a student’s experience at school and beyond. It is paramount for our students to feel empowered by their learning, to value and take responsibility for their learning and to demonstrate resilience.At ISD language learning permeates the entire school curriculum through authentic contexts in a culturally rich and diverse environment. Language development at ISD is the shared responsibility of all teachers, students and parents.Language development at ISD is the shared responsibility of all teachers, students and parents. We believe language is directly connected to identity and empowers students to understand, interpret and respond to ideas, attitudes and feelings. The development of language skills gives students the capacity to solve problems, think critically, work collaboratively and act creatively.At ISD all classrooms are multilingual. The language of instruction is English and all teachers communicate through and model this language. Students who are native speakers of English continue to develop their language skills through an academic context. Students who are non-native speakers of English are assessed and provided English language support as needed.Support is provided in class by the teachers, as well as through sessions with a specialised language teacher.As an IB school, ISD offers additional language learning. Multilingualism is considered a key advantage in a global world. ISD offers Spanish tuition with a native Spanish teacher. Classes are differentiated and content is tailored to suit native and non-native Spanish speakers. In addition, students’ mother tongues are highly valued and differentiated instruction promotes the use of native languages in everyday engagements. The Garrigues Labor and Employment Law service boasts a team of professionals with proven experience and is a leader in all labor and employment law specialties in the countries in which it operates. We advise on all labor, employment and social security specialties. Our advisory services are characterized by our professional commitment to our clients, our service vocation, our involvement and knowledge of the business of each sector and each client, the constant search for innovative and custom solutions, with a practical and strategic focus that delivers added value, and our cross-cutting and insightful approach. The excellence of our extensive labor and employment team and its broad expertise secure our position at the forefront of business law advisory services and value-added legal practice and know-how. We are also opinion makers and innovators. We harness the latest technologies to expedite our work and facilitate interaction with clients. Our services Comprehensive advice Employment contracts (ordinary and senior management); compensation and benefits; social security contributions; internal policies and protocols (remote working, recording of working time, digital disconnection, use of IT systems and work tools, policies to prevent bullying and sexual harassment, corporate social responsibility, whistleblowing and labor-related compliance, etc.); work/life balance; supplementary employee welfare; flexible working measures; international assignments; occupational risk prevention. Business restructuring Design and implementation of temporary and definitive measure to secure the future viability of businesses (collective dismissals, temporary layoffs (ERTE), RED mechanisms, voluntary redundancy plans, etc.) Litigation Defense of client interests at all instances and in all matter brought before the labor and judicial review courts. Collective bargaining Collective labor agreements and company agreements, standardization of conditions, material modification of working conditions, collective transfers, etc. Effective equality and diversity measures Equality plans, sexual and gender-based harassment protocols, and other policies and measures to promote equal treatment and opportunities in the workplace, shared parental responsibility, and to enable employees to balance their personal, family and work life. Labor due diligence Review of compliance with labor and employment law, whether as a preventive measure or as a result of corporate transactions. Labor aspects of corporate sustainability and due diligence strategies and ESG compliance Preparation of policies and evaluation of steps and measures to be implemented by companies. Advice on the preparation, implementation and review of the due diligence procedure and compliance with labor-related ESG criteria. Previous search terms close Cancel Home Services Tax Global mobility Global mobility For companies operating globally, ensuring that employees can quickly relocate to new destinations when needed is essential. However, practical arrangements can be complex, consuming both time and resources. Share Empower your talent to move Global mobility encompasses much more than traditional long-term assignments. We offer flexible solutions that support you globally in the management of the entire lifecycle of working abroad. Short-term project work, international business travel, multi-country employment scenarios, and cross-border remote work all require careful planning and coordination. Even a few days of work abroad can result in unexpected paperwork and navigating complex visa and work permit processes.The success of permanent transfers always requires careful planning, whether the destination is Finland or another country. Personal taxation, work permits, social security considerations, and other logistical factors must be addressed in advance. This ensures your business can adapt quickly to changing circumstances without unexpected complications. We take care of everything from work permits and assignment agreements to settling in. In addition, we can make cost estimations and address salary issues so that the transfer abroad goes smoothly from start to finish. Paula Holmström Head of People Services KPMG in Finland mail call Would you like to learn more about our services and experts? Contact us Comprehensive management of international assignments Outsourcing the management of international assignments to us ensures smooth operations and regulatory compliance, no matter where in the world your business takes place. Support throughout the entire lifecycle of international assignments Outsourcing and processes for assignment management Work permits and other documentation International assignment training Project assignments and international business travel International taxation, social security, and labor law (PWD) Settling-in services Technologies and automation that support mobility Global mobility services International taxation, social security, labor law (PWD), payroll, and other employer obligations Where should taxes be paid? How should social security be organized, and what employer obligations need to be considered? These are just a few of the questions an employer must answer when preparing to send talent to a new destination. Here are some of the things we can help with We determine the local employment terms and minimum wage requirements in each destination country. We manage the posting of worker notifications across Europe in a centralized and cost-effective manner. We help manage compliance risks related to regulatory changes in posting notifications. We can represent your company in the destination country. We assess employee tax burdens and advise on the taxation of various benefit packages. We address social security-related questions for employees. Project assignments, international business travel, and remote work Managing key employer obligations can be both challenging and time-consuming. Employers need detailed information on tax and salary payments, as well as registration requirements in the destination country. Additionally, staying informed about work permits and the implications of corporate taxes is crucial.We assist in the overall management of projects, create project guidelines tailored to your needs, and help identify potential risks related to business travel. Work and residence permits Our permit services are designed to ease the process of obtaining work and residence permits and facilitate a smooth transition to a new work environment. We offer a comprehensive range of services which can be individually tailored to help employees, and their families navigate the permit processes.Our service include for exampleAssessing the necessary permits, timelines, and documentation requirementsHandling required translations and legalizationsEvaluating additional regulatory registrations for entry into the country Relocating and settling-in Adapting to a new environment takes time, as each country has unique practices regarding authorities, housing, schooling, and childcare. That’s where we come in. We offer comprehensive global solutions for international assignments and recruitment. With the help of our settling-in service, employees and their families moving to Finland or abroad receive support for the beginning of their stay, and day-to-day matters get a kick-start. Our services include for exampleOrganizing employee's familiarization visit to the destination cityAssisting in finding housingArranging the move and supporting family members, from spousal assistance to locating school and daycare placements for childrenOther individual settling-in services Moving talent to Finland? See how we make it smooth. International assignment training With our coaching services, employers can support their employees and their families in adapting to the new work environment and country. Such permit may be obtained through an application process which is initiated prior to the candidate travelling to Sweden. To be granted a work permit, the prospective employee is required to have (i) a signed employment contract, (ii) valid passport, (iii) an offer of employment with terms at least on par with those set by Swedish collective agreements or which are customary within the occupation or industry. , (iv) a salary of at least SEK 27,360 per month before taxes (amount is correct until summer 2024, as amount updates every year in summer) and (v) have insurances covering health, life, employment and pension once the employment commences. Such insurances are provided by the prospective employer. For short-term assignments (less than three months) both work permission and a visa are required for citizens from certain countries. Some candidates, depending on their occupation, may be subject to certain exemptions from the work permit requirement. Previous may, inter alia, include concern specialists in an international corporation who work temporarily in Sweden for the corporation for less than 90 days and researchers or teachers in higher education who work for a maximum total of three months over a period of 12 months. Even if exempt from the work permit requirements, citizens of certain countries may still require an entry visa in order to travel to Sweden. Also, employment lasting longer than three months require an application for a residence permit for visits must in addition. Employers are obliged to notify the Swedish Tax Agency when a citizen from a country outside of EU/EEA or Switzerland is employed or sent here to work. Notification must be made regardless of whether the employment is for a shorter or longer period. Please further note that employers have an obligation to provide information to the Swedish Migration Agency of any changes made to the conditions of an offered employment in cases where a candidate has been granted a work permit. ICT (Intra Corporate Transfer) permits Citizens of a country outside of EU/EEA and Switzerland, who are employed in a country outside of EU/EEA and Switzerland, can apply for an ICT permit, which allows temporarily intra- corporate transfers. The ICT permit is applicable to managers, specialists and graduate trainees who are working more than 90 days in Sweden Further, the applicant must have been employed for at least three continuous months before the relocation. To obtain an ICT-permit, employer must offer employment conditions that are at least at the same level as Swedish collective agreements or what is customary in the profession or industry. The employer must also provide a copy of the employment contract. A decision on an ICT permit should be made within 90 days, and the decision must be issued before the applicant travels to Sweden. Residence permit for highly qualified candidates A Swedish residence permit has recently been introduced for highly qualified candidates with an advanced degree. Such residence permit maybe granted for a minimum of three months and a maximum of nine months for those who wish to visit Sweden to look for employment or investigate possibilities of starting a business in Sweden. In order to be granted such permit the applicant must (i) have completed studies equivalent to an examination at a higher level, (ii) have sufficient funds for accommodation in Sweden and for the return journey, and (iii) have a comprehensive health insurance valid in Sweden. If a third country national is offered employment or intends to start a business in Sweden during the permit period, they may apply from within Sweden either for a residence permit for work or a residence permit to start a business in Sweden. Employment Immigration (rather long-term or indefinite, local contract and social security) National Swedish work permit A third- country national who wants to work in Sweden requires a work permit. Such permit may be obtained through an application process which is initiated prior to the candidate travelling to Sweden. To be granted a work permit, the prospective employee is required to have (i) a signed employment contract, (ii) valid passport, (iii) an offer of employment with terms at least on par with those set by Swedish collective agreements or which are customary within the occupation or industry, (iv) a salary of at least SEK 27,360 per month before taxes (amount is correct until summer 2024, as amount updates every year in summer) and (v) have insurances covering health, life, employment and pension once the employment commences. Such insurances are provided by the prospective employer. Employers are obliged to notify the Swedish Tax Agency when a citizen from a country outside of EU/EEA or Switzerland is employed or sent here to work. Please further note that employers have an obligation to provide information to the Swedish Migration Agency of any changes made to the conditions of an offered employment in cases where a candidate has been granted a work permit. Once the work permit holder has worked and lived in Sweden for a total of four years over the past seven years, they may be granted a permanent residence permit. EU Blue Card Citizens of a non-EU country who have been offered a highly qualified position can apply for an EU-Blue card. An EU Blue Card issued in Sweden gives the holder the right to live and work in Sweden. In order to be granted an EU Blue Card, applicants need to (i) hold either a Swedish university degree (or a recognized or comparable foreign university degree) or five years of relevant professional experience, and (ii) have a job offer for highly qualified employment in Sweden, lasting minimum one year and with a monthly salary of at least one and a half times bigger than an average salary in Sweden. Lastly (iii) the applicant must have in place a comprehensive health insurance that is valid for care in Sweden. Further, to obtain an EU Blue Card, the employer must offer conditions that are at least at the same level as Swedish collective agreements or what is customary in the profession or industry. After five years with an EU Blue Card in Sweden (or another EU-country) status as long-term resident can be given if the Blue Card holder has been living in the same EU country for the last two years. The status as long-term resident gives some of the rights that an EU citizen has, including free movement in the EU. An EU Blue Card holder who has worked and lived in Sweden for 48 months, may be granted a permanent residence permit. At RNL Law, we provide a comprehensive expat legal service that ensures a smooth transition for both individuals and businesses. From securing work permits to finalizing housing contracts and ensuring compliance with Danish and EU employment laws, we manage the entire process for you. ​ Our Expat Legal services include: Visa and work permit applications; Review and drafting expat contracts; Housing agreements; and more With our holistic approach, we focus on making your move stress-free while protecting your legal rights. Let us help you or your employees settle confidently in Denmark. ​ See our specific services belowWork Permits and Visa Applications Work permits: RNL Law can assist companies in obtaining work permits for foreign employees, ensuring full compliance with Danish and EU regulations. Visa applications: Guidance on residency permits for expats, covering both short-term and long-term relocation to Denmark. Send in your caseRelocation Legal Assistance Relocation: Offering legal support to expats moving to Denmark, covering all aspects of relocation, including housing contracts, and compliance with local laws. Immigration Compliance: Ensuring companies are fully compliant with Danish immigration laws when relocating staff, avoiding legal pitfalls related to employment and residency regulations. Send us an emailEmployment Contracts for Expats Contracts: Drafting and reviewing expat-specific employment contracts that cover essential elements such as salary, benefits, relocation costs, and termination clauses. Equality and rights: Advising on employee rights and benefits specific to expatriates, such as healthcare, pension schemes, and leave policies. Send us an emailFamily Integration Services Family reunification: Legal guidance for bringing family members of expats to Denmark, including family reunification visas and schooling options for children. Family integration: Assistance with navigating Denmark’s family support systems and ensuring that expat families are fully integrated into the local community. Send us an emailExit Strategies and RepatriationTermination processes: Advising on termination or contract end, ensuring expats are aware of their legal rights regarding severance packages, pensions, and when leaving Denmark or their employer. Continue reading close What EY can do for you Modern workforce mobility functions are now required to address different needs and challenge old assumptions as they’re faced with dynamic economic, geopolitical regulatory, immigration, legal and health challenges. It’s not enough to rest on legacy mobility models rooted solely in business travel or long-term relocation. Mobility functions have increased scope and have taken on a more digital, integrated and strategic purpose. With this reality, mobility functions need to evolve to be high-impact, efficient, and cost-effective while helping to achieve business growth. The race for talent requires organizations to broaden their global talent strategy with a renewed sense of purpose and responsibility in navigating cross-border risks. Read More Read Less Open image description Close image description An interactive graphic showing the five drivers of a more evolved mobility function, including strategic alignment, talent linkage digital focus, flexibility, and use of external expertise. The EY People Mobility practice believes that people experience is as important as the process. Our professionals focus on improving employee experience through the exceptional and the routine, teaming to provide scalable cross-border and cross-functional services that support your talent strategy and business goals. We’re there for the journeys that transform your people, and your organization. Read More Read Less Open image description Close image description An interactive quiz to give respondents an idea of how “evolved” their mobility function might be, based on the five drivers of evolved mobility. Core mobility services Mobility should be woven into broader business and HR imperatives, rather than a stand-alone, transactional function. Human-centered Mobility programs that focus on the overall people experience while staying on top of global regulatory requirements, can be vital in talent attraction and retention. By blending the right people experience with the right technology, Mobility can evolve to support a workforce transformation that delivers a whole that is bigger than its parts. Immigration Today’s top talent represents a diverse range of cultures, nationalities and backgrounds. Organizations need to be able to rely on an efficient, well-executed process that honors diverse company cultures, retains quality output and manages compliance risk. Making this process seamless and worry free, with high-touch communications and consistent employee-focused experience, supports a global workforce strategy that is comprehensive and resilient. Read More Read Less EY Mobility Pathway Read More Read Less Cross-border work Business travel and hybrid working deliver learning and development opportunities that foster a collaborative growth mindset, increase employee engagement, and contribute to your talent attraction and retention goals. However, if not done right, cross-border work can quickly turn from a talent enabler to a talent obstacle. Evolved cross-border work programs focus on employee experience, process, policy, and alignment with your company’s technology ecosystem. These components, paired with technology solutions, keep EY and our clients, ahead of the ever-changing regulatory requirements and support sustainability efforts enable quicker speed to ground, manage cost and risk, and promote personal and professional development that can be career defining and market differentiating. Mobility managed services Given growing global regulatory complexity and continued geopolitical uncertainty, as well as increased scrutiny of the value and return from mobility, the only way that mobility teams can respond to all business needs is to strategically engage external expertise. With external vendors, organizations can alleviate some of the burden of transactional activities. Managed services capability allows you to do more with less, consolidating and optimizing data, operations and vendors to promote flexibility, agility and resilience. Expatriate tax - Sweden Expatriate tax - Sweden Global expatriate tax guide 01 Jan 2025 14 min read This publication provides a high level overview of the tax, social security and work permit regulatory compliance requirements for expatriates engaged to work in Sweden. Contents Expatriates taking up employment in Sweden will be subject to comprehensive rules and in some cases, employment visa requirements. Grant Thornton Sweden’s Global Mobility team can help employers and their expatriates to deal withSwedish tax and social security. In particular, Grant Thornton Sweden can help to identify Swedish tax planning opportunities and review tax equalization policies; as well as providing compliance services regarding Swedish tax filing requirements. Click on each of the areas below to expand for more information: Facts and figures Pre arrival procedures An individual from a non-EU/EEA country must as a main rule apply and be granted residency and a work permit at the Swedish Embassy or consulate general in his/her home country before arrival to Sweden. Registration for tax and residence purposes An individual should register for population purposes with the local tax office, if the assignment is expected to last for more than one year. The individual will then be receiving a normal tax identification number. If the expected stay is less than one year but continuous for more than six months, an individual should apply for income tax purposes resulting in a co-ordination number (TIN) being assigned to the individual. If the individual is to work in Sweden for less than six months, there is a possibility to apply for a Special Income Tax for non-resident individuals (SINK), see more below. Also with SINK, the individual will receive a co-ordination number for income tax purposes. Employment visas Nordic citizens are not required to apply for a work permit or a residence permit. An EU/EEA citizen arriving in Sweden with the intention to stay for more than three months may have to apply for a residence card at the Swedish Migration Board. A work permit is, however, not required for EU/EEA citizens. Tax year The tax year is the calendar year, 1 January to 31 December. Tax returns and compliance The taxpayer is liable to submit an individual income tax return by 2 May the year after the income year. Final tax assessment statements will be sent out continuously and latest in December. The employer shall withhold preliminary tax on employment income, i.e., Pay As You Earn (PAYE). The preliminary PAYE tax is based on annual tax tables prepared by the Tax Agency, unless SINK is approved. From 2021, it will no longer be possible for the employee to manage the employment tax payments themselves. Instead, the foreign employer must register as an employer and manage the reports and tax payments to the Swedish Tax Agency, even if there is no Swedish PE for CIT purposes. In addition, foreign businesses that have employees working in Sweden or conduct business in Sweden should apply for F-tax. Otherwise, Swedish companies are obliged to withhold 30% tax on invoices from foreign companies that carries out work in Sweden. Income tax rates- 2025 Income tax in Sweden consists of municipal and state tax. Municipal tax on salary income varies by municipality from approximately 29% to 35%. On taxable income exceeding SEK 643,100, state tax of 20 % is added. Taxable income (SEK) Municipal tax (%) State tax (%)17,300* – 643,100 29 – 35% –643,100 + 29 – 35% 20% * Minimum basic deduction (highest is SEK 45,300) Sample income tax calculation Income/Reduction SEKEmployment incomeSalary 800,000Car benefit 58,900Total earned income 858,900Basic deduction -17,300Taxable income: 843,500Capital income Dividend 2500Bank interest 1,000Interest on loan -15,000Total capital income/expense -11,500Income tax thereon Municipal income tax 843,500 * 31% 261,485State tax: (843,500 – 643,100) * 20% 40,080Capital tax reduction: (-11,500 * 30%) -3,450General pension contribution 45,500Tax reduction on general pension contribution -45,500Tax reduction on employment income -30,365Total tax 267,750 Basis of taxation Charge to tax Taxation of expatriates moving to Sweden is based on the length of their stay. A Swedish tax resident is liable under domestic legislation to pay tax in Sweden based on worldwide income at ordinary income tax rates. A non-resident individual is subject to tax in Sweden on source income only. SINK-taxation of 25% is applicable on certain Swedish sourced income e.g. employment and pension income. An application for SINK must be submitted to and approved by the Tax Agency for it to apply. A bilateral or multilateral income tax treaty may limit the right for Sweden to impose tax on certain types of income. Residence An individual will be considered a Swedish resident for tax purposes if: the individual is domiciled in Sweden, i.e., has his/her actual and permanent home in Sweden, or the individual stays in Sweden continuously for more than six months or on a regularly occurring stay in Sweden (short stays abroad for holidays, etc. are disregarded). The tax liability will apply from the first day. There are no explicit rules in Swedish tax law governing what would constitute a continuous stay in Sweden. However, the Swedish Tax Agency’s opinion is that an individual who regularly stays overnight in Sweden in a consecutive period exceeding six months should be considered resident in Sweden. It should be noted that an individual could be deemed to stay in Sweden regularly where the stay in total does not exceed six months but is considered to be “continuous and recurring”. An individual who has been domiciled in Sweden may be considered tax resident in Sweden also after a move from Sweden in case (s)he maintains so called essential connections with Sweden, e.g. earlier permanent home is maintained, or family resides in Sweden. Income from employment Generally, all earnings deriving from an activity, occasionally or regularly, are taxed as income from employment provided that the income is not considered business income or income from capital. All earnings from an employer to an employee are reportable and taxable as income from employment, i.e., wages, fees, sickness allowances, severance pay as well as benefits in kind i.e., free meals, a company car, interest free loans, travel benefits and expense allowances, e.g. subsistence allowances and travel compensation. Source of employment The source of employment income follows the OECD model treaty which means that the source of employment is generally determined by the place where services are performed. Benefit in kind In principle, all fringe benefits, i.e., any remuneration in kind received by an employee from the employer for services rendered, are taxable at their fair market value. For most common forms of fringe benefits there are standardized valuations set annually by the Swedish Tax Agency. Expatriate concessions Under certain conditions, foreign key employees working in Sweden for limited periods can qualify for a reduction of the income tax liability on their earnings. There are two alternatives for the tax relief to be applicable. One, if the gross monthly salary exceeds one and a half times the price base amount. The price base amount is SEK 58,800 (2025). If work begins in 2025, the monthly salary must be at least SEK 88,201. Two, if the employee is considered as an expert, a researcher or a key employee. The reduction amounts to 25% and is applicable only if the employer/employee has applied for a ruling within three months after the work started in Sweden. The tax relief applies for seven years from the start of the employee’s stay in Sweden. An individual who has been resident in Sweden during any of the five years prior to the start of the assignment in Sweden cannot qualify for tax relief status. The individual may not be a Swedish citizen. The tax relief exempts the following remuneration from Swedish tax and social security contributions: 25% of salaries and benefits moving to and from Sweden two holiday trips per year to the employee´s home country together with family members children’s school fees. Relief for foreign taxes Sweden has signed tax treaties with a large number of countries to avoid or relieve double taxation of income. An individual may be considered as tax resident in Sweden and in another country at the same time. For Swedish tax purposes, residency in another country does not affect Swedish residency. However, if Sweden has a tax treaty with the other country that claims residency, tax reliefs are available. In addition, Swedish internal tax laws allow reliefs to avoid double taxation on income, provided certain conditions are met. Deductions from taxable income All taxpayers with unlimited tax liability are entitled to a basic deduction, provided that 90% of the salary income is taxable in Sweden. This adjustment is made automatically by the Tax Agency when assessing the final taxes. The tax-free basic deduction amount ranges from SEK 17,300-45,300 depending on the total taxable income (or SEK 24,900 for the lowest taxable income). All taxpayers with unlimited tax liability and an income from employment are entitled to a tax reduction on employment income. The tax reduction is only deductible on municipal income tax and not state tax, real estate tax or property tax. Expenses, that are wholly, exclusively, and necessarily incurred in the performance of duty may be deducted from employment income if claimed in the income tax return. Expenses of this kind include, for example: additional living expenses during business travel or temporary assignment. travel expenses to and from work. the cost of using a personal car for business purposes. other costs which are necessary to perform the taxpayer’s duty. Some of these costs must exceed a certain amount in order to be deductible. Others are only deductible up to a certain maximum limit or under special circumstances. Employee mandatory foreign social security contributions are, with certain limitations, also deductible if the income is subject to income tax in Sweden. Other taxes Personal asset / capital tax Interest income, dividends and capital gains are taxed at a flat rate of 30%. Generally, 70% of capital losses are deductible. A tax reduction is granted on losses exceeding income on capital, resulting in a net loss. The reduction is 30% of the net loss up to SEK 100,000 and 21% on amounts exceeding SEK 100,000. Inheritance, estate, and gift taxes There is no gift or inheritance tax in Sweden. Investment income See ‘Personal asset tax’ above. Local taxes Not applicable, except municipality tax on employment/pension income. Real estate tax A municipal charge is levied on family houses instead of real estate tax. The charge varies depending on the type of house and construction year. The amount of property charge is calculated at 0.75% of the property´s assessment value in 2025, up to an upper limit of SEK 10,074 per residential building. Family houses abroad are not subject to the municipal charge. Real estate tax is still levied on other property, e.g., undeveloped land. Social security taxes The statutory social security charges amount to 31.42% (2025) of the total remuneration paid to employees including all taxable benefits in kind. Employees do not contribute to these charges and are only payable by the employer. Further, an employer pays, on average, an additional 24.26% of salaries to cover the cost of contractual pension plans. Employees are charged a pension insurance fee of 7% of employment income. The maximum charge is SEK 45,500 (for income year 2025). The charge is fully credited so this has no real effect on the income tax payments for the employee. The social security charges for foreign employers without a permanent establishment in Sweden is reduced to 19.8% (2025). A foreign employer without a permanent establishment in Sweden can agree with the employee, that the employee will pay the social security costs on the employer’s behalf. The employee has to file an application and register with the Tax Agency to pay monthly contributions under such agreement. However, please note that this is less common after the legislation update during 2021 that foreign employers are obliged to register as an employer and report and pay the income taxes. It is then easier if the foreign employer also reports the social security contributions. Stock options Stock options classified as employee stock options according to Swedish legislation are generally taxed as employment income upon exercise. The taxable benefit is equal to the difference between the fair market value of the stock on the date of exercise, and the option (exercise) price. As the tax treatment of equity-oriented plans is complex in Sweden, and the classification of each plan is very important, we strongly recommend that this issue is discussed with a Grant Thornton Sweden tax specialist. Wealth tax There is no wealth tax in Sweden. Other specific taxes An individual who is not a member of the Swedish Church, or some other specific Church, still has to pay a burial fee. The fee depends on the municipality and the average burial fee is 0.293% (income year 2025). and assignees. Find your home with Relocare, not just a place to live! Finding a place to live, packing, moving and all the in-betweens. Relocation to Denmark is a big decision and finding a home as an expat is a real challenge – especially on the legal aspects. Relocare is the leading relocation agent on the housing market, taking care of all the housing details, helping you through the entire process when searching for your new home and lets you concentrate on your job. We can take you on a guided tour to see houses or apartments, based on your wishes and budget, and present you with as many selections as you need – to find the home where you belong. The rental market in especailly Copenhagen and Aarhus is very difficult and fast moving, but we have the knowledge, network and legal experience to help you to select and move into your new rented house or apartment. Relocare can also help you to purchase a house or an apartment, depending on your wishes for a home when relocating to Denmark. Once we find you the right home, we will also assist you with the negotiation of the lease, terms and price when renting an apartment or a house. The Danish rental act is quite complex, and is properly one of the most comprehensive in Europe. It gives the landlords options to claim restoration and we take very much care, that you will not be held responsible for any claims which are not legal, or your fault when you move out. If you’re buying accommodation in Denmark, we will also help you to investigate if it is the best option for you. If it is we will find the right home and we use experts to sort out legal matters. We want to be sure that this important housing task becomes as easy and convenient for you as possible when moving and relocating to Denmark. We have substantial experience finding the best houses and apartments for expats. Expertise that will also be of help to you when negotiating legal terms and prices for your chosen accommodation in Denmark. Relocare is strong on the legal aspects, and very often we save expat’s for several thousands of kroner for especially rental apartments. Mainly due to our strong knowledge and experience with the Danish rental law – one of the most complex laws of it’s kind in Europe. The law is applied both for the rental contract, but also for the move-in report and Relocare have saved expats and companies thousands of crones on this part alone. It doesn’t matter if you are living in Copenhagen, Aarhus, Odense or any other city. We will be there to assist you as an expat or returning Dane with your housing, helping you to find the home of your dreams. Relocare covers all of Denmark and have helped hundreds of expats successfully through the years. Also in midsized towns like Roskilde, Vejle and Esbjerg, where the conditions might be different and the rental housing proces harder to manage than in the larger cities due to the very limited supply of mainly furnished homes. The rental descriptions might for example not be available in English. But we will always ensure, that you get the best housing option that fits for your preferred home when moving and relocating to Denmark. Please contact us for an offer suitable to your wishes and needs for housing. rows.content: SEARCH MENU CLOSE SEARCH MENU CLOSE +353 1 912 5961 info@propsupport.com Case Studies International Secondees Our Approach How We’re Different What We Do About Us Our Values Organisations we serve Landlords Organisations News & Insights Contact PropSupport Home » News & Insights » Top Relocation Companies in Ireland: A Complete Guide for HR and Business Leaders Top Relocation Companies in Ireland: A Complete Guide for HR and Business Leaders 04 October 2024 Introduction Relocating employees to Ireland can be a complex process, and many companies rely on experienced relocation firms to ensure a smooth transition. The challenge for companies can be identifying the firms that best fit their needs, given the somewhat fragmented nature of the Irish relocation market. Unlike other professional services where established brand names (such as top legal and accounting firms) dominate, the relocation sector features many specialised companies, making the decision process more challenging. This guide provides a comprehensive list of the top relocation companies in Ireland, offering a wide range of services from housing assistance to settling-in support. Whether your organisation is relocating senior executives, junior staff, or simply supporting existing employees with housing issues, choosing the right relocation partner is crucial for employee satisfaction. In this guide, we’ll also highlight how PropSupport’s unique focus on housing solutions sets it apart from traditional relocation companies, offering a modern alternative tailored to the needs of junior staff and cost-conscious organisations. The Fragmented Irish Relocation Market – Traditional Relocation Companies and Newcomers The Irish relocation market is a diverse and fragmented landscape, with many companies offering a wide range of services to assist individuals and businesses moving to Ireland. Most traditional relocation companies focus heavily on comprehensive packages, including physical moving, visa arrangements, and settling-in support, particularly for senior executives. While these services are essential for many businesses, they can come with a high cost and may not always be required by every employee. Below is a list, in no particular order, of 10 relocation companies in Ireland that provide a broad range of Irish relocation services to help you or your employees relocate smoothly. 1. Onboard Ireland Onboard Ireland offers end-to-end corporate relocation services, including home finding, school search, and settling-in support. Their expertise lies in managing large-scale employee mobility programs across Ireland and Europe, making them an ideal choice for multinational companies looking to relocate staff quickly and efficiently. 2. The Relocations Company The Relocations Company provides more than just logistical support—they offer holistic relocation services that address the personal and professional challenges of moving. Their focus on employee wellbeing during transitions makes them a great option for companies seeking a thoughtful approach to relocation. 3. PropSupport PropSupport is not a traditional relocation company. Instead, it offers housing-specific support for companies looking to help junior staff members relocate without the high costs associated with full-service relocation packages. Utilising a modern, technology-enabled approach, PropSupport focuses on housing search, scam prevention, and rental support. It also empowers employees to conduct their own searches, providing a flexible dual approach: guided support combined with self-service tools. 4. Irish Relo IrishRelo is known for its comprehensive global employee relocation services. Their core strengths lie in home finding, school search, and area orientation, making them a great choice for businesses that need a well-rounded relocation experience. They provide detailed settling-in services to help employees and their families acclimate quickly. 5. Ireland Relocations Ireland Relocations focuses on corporate mobility programs, offering a strong suite of services that cater to the needs of key employees moving to European operations. With a focus on housing, visa services, and compliance, they ensure smooth transitions for international employee moves. 6. SettleIn Settle In provides flexible relocation services tailored to the needs of corporate clients, families, and individuals. Their family-friendly services help relocating families with everything from school searches to cultural orientation programs, ensuring an easy transition for both employees and their loved ones. 7. Cornerstone Relocation Group Cornerstone stands out for its local expertise in Dublin and Cork, combined with a global approach. They offer a balance of global mobility services and local insight, making them ideal for companies relocating employees to Ireland who need in-depth knowledge of the local market. 8. Corporate Care Relocation Corporate Care Relocation specialises in relocating professionals to the UK and Ireland, offering high-quality, personalized services. Their relocation packages range from housing to visa support, and they are known for their award-winning service that ensures employees settle quickly and efficiently. 9. Celtic Relocations Celtic Relocations focuses on bespoke relocation solutions for individuals and families moving to Ireland. They offer tailored services, whether securing temporary accommodation or arranging long-term housing, ensuring each client’s specific needs are met with precision. 10. Executive Relocations Ireland Executive Relocations Ireland caters to high-end, executive relocations, offering premium services like home finding, school enrollment, and cultural integration. They are particularly adept at managing complex moves for senior executives, making them a top choice for businesses relocating leadership staff. How to Select and Evaluate Relocation Company Offerings Choosing the right relocation company in Ireland involves understanding your organisation’s specific needs and the profiles of the employees being relocated. Here are some key factors to consider when evaluating relocation companies: 1. Employee Demographics: Start by mapping out the profiles of the employees you’re relocating. Are they senior executives requiring comprehensive relocation services (including visa support, school enrollment, and physical moving), or junior staff needing primarily housing support? Understanding this distinction will help narrow down your options. 2. Scope of Services: Determine whether you need Irish relocation services that include a full range of offerings (such as visa arrangements, moving logistics, and settling-in services) or whether a housing-specific solution like PropSupport may be sufficient for your employees. Would PropSupport’s light package consisting of guided support combined with self-service tools suffice for younger renters who are comfortable searching independently? 3. Budget Considerations: For more senior staff, businesses may have a higher relocation budget, making comprehensive packages from traditional relocation companies in Ireland appropriate. However, for junior staff or employees with lighter relocation needs, cost-effective housing solutions, such as those offered by PropSupport, can help minimise costs while still providing critical support. 4. Flexibility: Consider whether the relocation company allows flexibility in payment arrangements (e.g., whether employees can pay directly for some services) and in the scope of support offered. By carefully evaluating these factors, your organisation can select the right relocation assistance to ensure a smooth, efficient transition for employees. Why Choose PropSupport for Housing Support PropSupport offers a range of housing support services to new or existing employees. Our service packages range from light offerings comprising of consultation and security tools versus full comprehensive service offeirngs including all aspects of search, support and security. Here’s why PropSupport is worth considering for housing support: PropSupport offers tailored housing support services for both new and existing employees. Our service packages range from light offerings, which include consultation and security tools, to comprehensive packages that cover all aspects of housing search, support, and security. Here’s why PropSupport is a strong choice for housing support. 1. Cost-effective: Unlike traditional relocation companies that focus on full-service packages, PropSupport specialises in affordable housing solutions, particularly for junior staff. We offer flexible service options that make high-quality housing accessible without the high fees often associated with senior executive relocations. For those needing minimal assistance, our light support packages offer an even more budget-friendly option. 2. Complementary to Traditional Relocation Agents: We work with organisations that already have arrangements with traditional relocation agents but want to extend housing support to junior staff. PropSupport provides a housing-specific solution that works alongside existing services. 3. Housing Support as an Employee Perk: PropSupport’s services can also be offered to existing employees who require housing assistance, making it a valuable perk for all staff members—not just those who are relocating. 4. Modern, Tech-driven Solutions: Our technology-enabled platform simplifies the property search process. Employees can access a wide range of housing options online, with tools to filter properties based on their preferences. This tech-driven approach enhances both security and efficiency in finding suitable accommodation. 5. Flexible Payment Options: We offer flexible payment solutions, allowing companies to pay directly or enabling employees to handle the cost themselves. This ensures that businesses can provide housing support without creating additional administrative burdens. 6. Focus on Security: With rental scams becoming more common, PropSupport prioritises security by offering scam prevention tools, rental agreement preparation, and property risk assessments. This ensures that employees can secure safe, reliable housing. 7. Irish Owned and Operated: Irish Owned and Operated: Based in Dublin, PropSupport has a deep understanding of the Irish rental market. Our local expertise allows us to provide renters with insights and housing options that are perfectly suited to their needs. 8. FIND MY VISA Understanding the Spain Digital Nomad Visa Remote EmployeesIndividuals employed by companies based outside Spain who can carry out their work remotely. Freelancers and ContractorsSelf-employed individuals with various sources of income from clients outside Spain. Business OwnersEntrepreneurs who own businesses that do not require their physical presence outside Spain and can be managed remotely from Spain. Digital EntrepreneursThose who run online businesses or work in digital industries, provided they meet the income requirements. The Spain Digital Nomad Visa allows non-EU remote workers, including freelancers, entrepreneurs, and remote employees, to live and work legally in Spain while staying employed by foreign companies or serving international clients. It offers long-term residency and visa-free travel within the Schengen Area, making it ideal for digital professionals seeking a high quality of life with full location flexibility.To qualify, applicants must show sufficient remote income, hold private health insurance, and provide a clean criminal record. A Spain digital nomad visa lawyer ensures your application is complete, compliant, and submitted correctly — helping you avoid delays and move forward with confidence. Nationality Criteria The Digital Nomad Visa for Spain is available to citizens of countries outside the European Economic Area (EEA) and Switzerland. Check with your country of origin for visa eligibility. 2. Employment Duration Applicants must be employed at their current organization for at least three months. 3. Remote Work Authorization The company must issue a signed letter authorizing you to work remotely. All functions must be carried out from a remote location. 4. Company Establishment Duration The company you work for must have been incorporated for at least the last 12 months. 5. Freelancer and Entrepreneur Validation If you are a freelancer or a company owner, you must prove that you have had a commercial relationship with one or more companies for at least three months. 6. Criminal Record You must have a clean criminal record history. 7. Health Insurance As an employee of a company, you must have comprehensive health insurance coverage valid in Spain. 8. Registration Commitment for Self-Employed As a self-employed or business owner, you must register as self-employed in Spain once the permit is granted. 9. Financial Requirements You must show enough financial resources to support yourself and your family during your residency. This includes 200% of the monthly minimum wage (SMI) for yourself, plus 75% of the SMI for the first family member and 25% of the SMI for each additional family member.As of 2025, this would be €2,763 for the main applicant, an additional €1,036 for the first family member and €345 for each additional family member. 10. Restrictions on Company Location Companies authorizing remote work must be based outside Spain. Self-employed individuals or contractors can work for a Spanish company, but it must not exceed 20% of their total professional activity.
