October 2021 European Renters are Returning to France, the Bail Mobilité is in Progress, and Rents are Progressively Returning to Normal While the first months of 2021 were synonymous with a nuanced recovery for traditional furnished rentals, Lodgis unveils its barometer for the third quarter of 2021. The start of the school year, a key period for long-term furnished rentals, brings color back into the market September 2021 Did you know? Lodgis has been working in Lyon since 2019 and is now a leader in Lyon’s furnished rental market Since April 1, 2021, Lodgis, the leader in the French furnished rental market, has become a key actor in the market of Lyon by proposing almost 500 furnished properties for rent as a response to real needs in the market August 2021 Lodgis, the leader in the french furnished rental market, positions itself as a real competitor with their property management services Based on this trend and the growing need for solutions adapted to new housing uses, Lodgis is growing by offering multiple rental property management offers so that each property owner can chose, in full transparency, the option that is best adapted to their needs. July 2021 Lodgis' Barometer - Second Trimester of 2021 // Impacts of the health crisis: caution and recent increase in demand If the start of the quarter was more difficult with mobility still in its infancy, demand is now showing strong growth for the start of the September: in June 2021, Lodgis recorded an increase of 43% in rental requests compared to June 2020 and +18% compared to June 2019 April 2021 Traditional Furnished Rentals: The Recovery is Underway At the end of the first trimester of 2021, Lodgis, the leader of the Île-de-France region’s traditional furnished rental market, has published their assessment of the market for this period. Despite the still present context of the health crisis, which has had numerous impacts on this sector, the end is in sight and Lodgis is preparing for a strong summer period. February 2021 New Lifestyles, Flexibility, and Digitalization: The Unexpected Effects of the Pandemic on the Furnished Rental Market Shaken up by the health crisis, the furnished rental market has been able to reinvent itself and adapt. At the start of the year, Lodgis, the leader in furnished rentals in Ile-de-France, takes stock of 2020 and prepares for 2021... January 2021 Lodgis’ 2020 Furnished Rental Barometer // Hit but not sunk, the traditional furnished rental has been able to reinvent itself and become stronger Lodgis unveils its 2020 furnished rental barometer. If this year of health crisis necessarily impacted the real estate market, traditional furnished rentals have been able to reinvent themselves to succeed... October 2020 The Real Estate Market and the Health Crisis: Traditional Furnished Rentals Are Still Doing Well The 3rd trimester barometer from Lodgis, the leader in furnished rentals in the Ile-de-France region, discusses the most recent updates within the Parisian real estate market. If the real estate sector is still strongly impacted by the health crisis, all indicators also seem to show an increase in traditional furnished rentals... July 2020 Lowered rents, French tenants, students, and an increase in principle residence leases: The furnished rental market is picking up and reinventing itself A few weeks after de-confinement, Lodgis released their new barometerfor furnished rentals in Paris. The leader in furnished rentals in the Ile-de-France region draws up a progress report for the sector, which wasalso impacted by the recent pandemic... June 2020 EXPERT OPINION - The Traditional Furnished Rental Market Even Stronger… A Result of Being Digitized and Personalized! Alexis Alban, Deputy CEO of Lodgis, gives his perspective on France’s Furnished Rental Market just a few weeks after de-confinement. Even though traditional furnished rentals have managed to fare well during this crisis, the market has nevertheless had to reinvent itself. Alexis Alban sees a real opportunity to rethink this sector and the job description of a real estate agent. April 2020 Lodgis' message in response to Airbnb's fundraising announcement In response to AirBnB's announcement of a billion dollar fundraising effort in order to offer support for after the crisis, Alexis Alban, CEO of Lodgis, talks about the consequences of the pandemic on the real-estate market, but also about the American giant’s approach, which no longer represents the financial paradise that property owners had previously imagined. March 2020 Coronavirus Solidarity / “Housing for Medical Professionals”: Lodgis has called on our community of property owners As France has been affected by the Coronavirus pandemic over the past few weeks, French medical professionals fight daily to take care of those who are sick and to save lives. But in doing so, they are faced with complicated life and work conditions like long commutes to get to and from work and worry about contaminating their families and loved ones. In an attempt to show our support, Lodgis has called on our community of property owners to graciously offer their vacant furnished apartments to medical professionals free of charge for a month. January 2020 Lodgis barometer: in 2019, furnished rentals broke records It’s the beginning of the year and Lodgis is unveiling its annual recap of the traditional furnished rentals market in Paris. Its been a year of records for Lodgis: a large increase in the demand for furnished properties for rent, a growing interest in rental investment, and the clear success of the bail mobilité (mobility lease) for both owners and tenants. October 2019 Barometer of the furnished rental market in Paris – Q3 2019: Professionals in mobility are more and more attracted to furnished rentals The 3rd barometer of 2019 for Lodgis, a leader in the furnished rental market in the Ile-de-France area, reviews the latest market developments: a confirmed attraction to this type of accommodation for professionals in mobility and tenants of French nationality, the limited effects of rent control on prices and the confirmed success of the ‘Bail Mobilité’ (mobility lease). September 2019 20 after its creation, the leader Lodgis confirms its position as an expert and unveils its ambitions 20 years after its opening in Ile-de-France, Lodgis continues to grow based on its ability to adapt, offer services and the expertise of its teams: after opening its services this year to ‘Région’ (in particular Lyon, Toulouse and Bordeaux), Lodgis aims to stay one step ahead by continuing to reinvent itself in a constantly changing market. July 2019 Parisian furnished rental 2nd barometer of 2019 for Lodgis : furnished rentals more and more sought after by the French The 2nd barometer of 2019 for Lodgis confirms the trends of the real estate market outlined at the start of the year: there are more and more French tenants, a slight rise in rents in Paris and confirmed success of the ‘bail mobilité’. Success of the Bail Mobilité: nearly one thousand leases signed in 6 months [Infographics] Lodgis has made a first positive assessment of the Bail Mobilité, 6 months after it came into place: as of today, nearly 1000 rental leases have been signed. April 2019 Lodgis continues to grow and expands its services to Bordeaux, Lyon and Toulouse In the last 30 years, the share of furnished housing in the French private rental sector has more than doubled. Working with this trend, Lodgis is expanding its horizons, offering services to tenants and owners of furnished properties in Bordeaux, Lyon and Toulouse from the 24th April 2019 thanks to an online process and a team of expert advisors in these cities. Barometer of the furnished rental market in Paris - Q1 2019: Rents slightly up in Paris… and the success of the Bail Mobilité! The first 2019 Barometer of Lodgis shows a slight rent increase in Paris, and an enthusiastic reception of the Bail Mobilité which represents 30% of leases signed since the beginning of the year... January 2019 2018 Barometer of furnished rental market in Paris « As the Parisian furnished rental market remained stable in 2018, it should experience a real shake-up in 2019. Indeed, following the tightening of rules surrounding holiday rentals, and an increase in controls, owners are increasingly stopping seasonal renting in order to benefit from the traditional furnished renting... October 2018 The ELAN law: what are the consequences for furnished rentals? After a year of debate the ELAN law, development of housing, planning and digital is in the final stages of its legaslatif process. What will be the consequences for furnished rentals? With Lodgis, this is a return to two principle values, lease mobility and rent control. Barometer of furnished rentals in Paris – T3 2018 : Increase in the frequentation of students, especially young Europeans In Paris the average price of a furnished rental stabilises at €36.95 per m2, compared to €36.71 in the 3rd quarter of 2017. Therefore, rent remains steady and the price growth is inferior to that of inflation, which stood at 2.2% between September 2017 and September 2018. July 2018 Paris Furnished Rentals Barometer – Second Quarter 2018: Increase in visits by Europeans and in stays for professional reasons In Paris, the prices of furnished rentals have seen a slight increase during the second quarter of the year: €37.77 / m2 / month on average, which is an increase of +1.5% compared to the same period in 2017... April 2018 Paris furnished rentals barometer – 2018 first quarter In Paris, rents for furnished rentals increased slightly during the first quarter of the year: on average €36.71 per square metre, that is +1.1% compared with the same period in 2017... February 2018 Furnished Rentals in Paris: What are foreign residents looking for? Students, people travelling for business, expats… There are more and more foreigners coming to Paris and choosing to rent a furnished property for their stay capital. January 2018 Furnished Rentals in Paris: 2017 Barometer The furnished rental market is a stable market, which is essentially aimed at an international clientele, and this stability in rents should be confirmed in 2018, particularly thanks to an increase in the number of furnished properties. Changes to the real estate tax system in 2018 : Stability despite a few modifications The 2018 Finance Bill is developing the real estate tax system. What are the major changes ? What will be the consequences be on the market ? Maud Velter, Associate Director at Lodgis explains the situation. November 2017 Maud Velter's analysis of the implementation of registration numbers for furnished rentals for tourists in Paris from the 1st December Registration numbers will become mandatory on advertisements for furnished apartments for tourists from the 1st December 2017 in Paris, and will also come into effect in Bordeaux from the 1st March... October 2017 Paris furnished rentals barometer - 2017 third quarter: Europeans, the top tenants for furnished rentals in Paris In Paris, the price of furnished housing for rent has been stable throughout the third quarter of the year : 36.71€ per m² on average, a 0.5% increase in comparison with the same period in 2016... September 2017 Furnished rentals: who are the investors? Furnished or unfurnished rentals? More and more landlords are being drawn towards furnished rentals. The number of furnished rentals has almost tripled over the last 30 years, from 3.6% to 9.5%, in response to steadily growing demand. But who are landlords for furnished rentals? August 2017 30 years of ERASMUS: Helpful tips for renting to students studying abroad Every year France welcomes even more students from the European Union. To celebrate the 30th anniversary of the ERASMUS program, Lodgis, Parisian real estate agency specialized in furnished rentals, is sharing its helpful tips on the easiest way to rent a property. July 2017 Paris furnished rentals barometer - 2017 second quarter In Paris, the furnished rentals price are remaining steady throughout the second quarter of the year: €37,20 per square meter in average, that is to say + 0,7% compared to the same period in 2016... June 2017 Furnished rentals in Paris : Focus on Traveling students Lodgis, Parisian real estate agency specialized in furnished rentals, analyzed 1 078 bookings made during the second semester of 2016 in order to know more about students traveling to the capital. Here are the main conclusions of this survey. April 2017 Paris furnished rentals barometer / 2017 first quarter: +0,5%, prices remain steady in the capital! In Paris, the cost of furnished rentals is slightly increasing during the first quarter of the year: €36,97/sqm in average, that is to say +0,5% compared to the same period in 2016... Furnished rentals in Paris: Who are the traveling professionals? Lodgis, the Parisian real estate agency specialized in furnished rentals, analyzed 1 398 booking made during the second quarter of 2016 in order to know more about traveling professionals in the capital. Here is what came out of this inquiry. March 2017 [Opinion column] The ALUR law, 3 years later: The furnished rentals market sails on troubled waters Three years have passed since the law of March, 24th 2014's enactment. The text, which counts around 177 articles, develops a real legal arsenal intending to revolutionize the real estate market. What are the consequences of this “legal tsunami” on furnished rentals? How not to get lost in this string of regulations? And most importantly, how to reintroduce an equilibrium between lessors and tenants? January 2017 The owners of furnished rental properties only have few days left to change tax system! The renters of furnished apartments only have few days to change tax system and make important tax savings on the incomes they get from renting their properties... Paris furnished rentals survey 2016: Stable leasing... since 4 years ago 2016 was marked by a security environment particularly tensed in the Capital, which is characterized by a drop of foreign clients and a certain prices stagnation. Overall, the relation between supply and demand for furnished rentals barely evolves and experiences a small upward variation (+0,1% between 2015 and 2016). For 4 successive years, the price of Parisian furnished rentals is moving towards stability... December 2016 A study with furnished rental landlords in Paris Lodgis has conducted a close study with these landlords in the French capital to address the following: what are their financial interests, how have recent legislative changes affected their business activity, and who are they? Taxes: the LMNP (private landlord) status to save money Whilst taxpayers are desperately trying to reduce their tax bills via a range of different avoidance schemes, the status of Tenant of a Private Landlord (Loueur en Meublé Non Professionnel) is worth investigating. Lodgis offers advice on how to cut your tax bills via the online service jedeclaremonmeuble.com. November 2016 Dealing with damages to furnished rental properties: in theory and through case studies For both the landlord and the tenant, dealing with damages can often be a dreaded affair, as it represents both a long and costly procedure. Lodgis and the insurance broker, French Furnished Insurance, are both specialists in the furnished rental sector, offering theoretical advice and practical guidance based on frequent cases. October 2016 Barometers for furnished rentals in Paris / 3rd quarter 2016: The academic year begins with a slight fall in rents At -0.3% for the third quarter of 2016 compared with the same period last year, the cost of furnished rentals in Paris is slightly down. This trend is even more pronounced in the central arrondissements, where rents have fallen -1.7% since 2015... Lodgis now offers and integrates VR for all its 3D content Today, Lodgis, Real Estate Agency in Paris, announced its support of Matterport CoreVR, a simple option to add VR support to any Matterport 3D Space, creating the fastest, easiest, and least expensive end-to-end system for delivering a VR experience of a real-world place... September 2016 Living in Paris: how to choose the right neighborhood? Moving to Paris is often the beginning of a great adventure. Spread across 105.4km², the City of Light is a real mishmash of arrondissements with their individual styles and atmospheres. Lodgis focuses on the best neighborhoods in Paris to live in according to one's profile, tastes and budget. July 2016 [Opinion Column] The rent caps in Paris: important facts that should be noted The rental caps in Paris have been in place for almost a year. Let's take stock: has this key measure of the loi ALUR delivered on its promises? Furnished rental barometers in Paris / Data for the 2nd quarter of 2016: Rent stability is confirmed With a year-on-year increase of 1.3% for the second quarter of 2016, furnished rental prices in Paris are in line with the revised rent benchmarks. Indeed,the prefectoral decree ratified on June 17th has set new caps that cannot be exceeded as of August 1st 2016... June 2016 [Infographic] How to set the rental price for your furnished apartment in Paris? Following the introduction of rental caps in Paris, how should you set the rent for your furnished property? Here's an interactive explanation from Lodgis, the furnished rental specialists in Paris... ► View the infographic (in French) May 2016 3D revolutionises estate agency / You can now walk through a Lodgis apartment online with a virtual tour! The digital revolution reaches far beyond the bounds of the new technologies sector. Its effects are increasingly being felt in the real estate market. Parisian estate agency Lodgis now offers a virtual tour service for the sale properties on its books, and will soon be extending this to cover lets. Open the door and step right in! April 2016 2016 taxes: 3 May is the deadline for furnished-let landlords to declare their rental income under the income and expenditure regime It's spring again, and that means it's time for people in France to battle with their tax declarations - never an easy task! Amateur furnished-let landlords (LMNPs) have plenty of questions... ► Available in French. Established in 1940, we combine the academic rigour of the UK curriculum with the Spanish cultural foundations needed to thrive both locally and internationally. Our students achieve outstanding results in both international and Spanish examinations, progressing to highly selective universities in Spain, the UK, Europe and the USA — including institutions ranked among the world’s top 10 in the QS World University Rankings. Rated “Excellent in all areas” in four consecutive British Schools Overseas (BSO) inspections and ranked among the Best Schools in Spain by Forbes and ABC, our school offers a well-established, high-performing education. Sixth Form pathways include the bilingual BiBac® programme (El Colegio Británico – Bachillerato), designed to give students access to both Spanish and international university routes, alongside two globally recognised options: iA Levels (from 2026) and the IB Diploma (Candidate School 2027). Why Choose Our Private School in Pozuelo de Alarcon, Madrid? Spain's 1st British School The former British Council School was established over 85 years ago as the first British school in Spain, combining long-standing tradition with a respected British educational framework and membership of NABSS (National Association of British Schools in Spain). A Legacy of Excellence 4 consecutive “Excellent in all areas” BSO inspections and consistent ranking among Spain’s top schools reflect our commitment to high standards. We are also a White Rose Champion School (maths & science) and the only ABRSM Partner School in Spain for outstanding music provision. Real-World Readiness Students gain practical experience for their future endeavours through Year 11 work shadowing, leadership and entrepreneurship programmes, STEM projects, and expert university and careers guidance. Opportunities to earn certifications in 5 languages further expand their global pathways. Brilliant Student Outcomes Students at our bilingual school in Pozuelo achieve exceptional results in British and Spanish examinations, earning “Top in the World” awards for IGCSE exams. Graduates progress to leading universities, including Cambridge, MIT, Stanford, and top Spanish institutions. PreviousNext An International Education in Madrid That Turns Ambition into Achievement Outstanding Academic Performance Students at our private school in Pozuelo achieve exceptional academic outcomes, regularly receiving “Top in the World”, “Top in Europe”, and “Top in Spain” awards in Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE examinations. These distinctions recognise extraordinary performance across subjects including Chemistry, Physics, Economics, Biology, Mandarin, Spanish Language and Literature, and History. Our pupils also stand out in national and international science and mathematics Olympiads, showcasing their exemplary preparation. Leading University Destinations Strong academic results open doors to leading universities worldwide. 100% of our graduates progress to higher education, joining prestigious institutions such as Cambridge, Imperial College London, UCL, LSE, Yale, Stanford, UCLA, Georgia Tech, and MIT, as well as top Spanish universities including Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Universidad de Navarra, IE, and ESADE. Global Opportunities and Scholarships Beyond academics, many of our graduates stand out across the arts and sports, receiving full sports scholarships to universities in the United States and invitations to perform at major cultural events. Impressive Alumni Success Our alumni go on to succeed across business leadership, science and research, specialised engineering, medicine, law, the arts, aviation, and public life. Among them is Formula 1 driver Carlos Sainz, one of the school’s most distinguished alumni, reflecting the breadth of talent developed within our community. What could your child achieve with the right foundation? ENQUIRE NOW What Sets Our Private School in Pozuelo Apart Proven Academic Pathways Families choose The British School of Madrid for its established reputation, strong academic outcomes, and proven pathways to leading universities worldwide. Our motto, “Best of Both Worlds,” reflects the balance families seek: rigorous British academics alongside strong Spanish educational foundations. A dedicated team of 10 university guidance counsellors supports students from Years 10 to 13, helping them make informed subject choices and prepare applications that stand out. Students receive tailored guidance for universities in Spain, the UK, the United States, and across Europe, including SAT preparation and Oxbridge interview support. Those applying to Spanish universities are guided through the PAU route, with many students achieving grades above 11, essential for highly competitive degree programmes. Immersion in Languages At our international school in Pozuelo, English immersion begins at 12 months and continues throughout a student’s education. The British curriculum is delivered in English by native-speaking teachers, while Spanish curriculum elements ensure strong academic and cultural foundations in both languages. Beyond bilingualism, pupils can develop fluency in up to 5 languages. French and German are introduced as part of the curriculum, with Chinese available as an extracurricular option. Students also prepare for recognised international certifications, including Cambridge English (FCE, CAE, CPE), DELF/DALF, Goethe, and Chinese language examinations. Enrichment and Practical Skills Enrichment plays a central role at our private school in Pozuelo, with music as a key pillar. Students learn instruments from the early years through a structured programme, with opportunities to join ensembles, prepare for ABRSM and Rock School examinations, and perform regularly in both English and Spanish. Some of our students have progressed to advanced music studies and careers. A wide range of activities allows students to explore their interests and hone talents, including robotics, Cine Club (scriptwriting, filming, editing), and Elite Golf programmes. Competitive sports teams take part in local and regional leagues, regularly bringing home trophies that showcase their teamwork, determination, and discipline. World-readiness is built through practical experience. In Year 11, students complete a four-day work shadowing placement in a professional environment, alongside leadership initiatives, entrepreneurship programmes, STEM and research projects, and public speaking opportunities — helping them connect their education to future pathways. PreviousNext A Former British Council School Many families still know us by our former name, the British Council School. Today, as The British School - El Colegio Británico, we carry forward a heritage of educational excellence that began with our inception. Our private school in Pozuelo has educated generations of students and played an important role in the development of international education in Madrid. At its core is a commitment to exceptional teaching, strong academic standards, and a community built on the values of loyalty, flexibility, care, resilience, and challenge. This enduring legacy is reflected in a rigorous academic programme, excellent pastoral care, and a clear focus on preparing students for life beyond school. For families, it provides the reassurance that their child is in safe hands throughout their educational journey — and is why we are widely recognised as one of the best schools in Pozuelo and Madrid. Academic Stages at The British School of Madrid From Early Years to Sixth Form, students at our private school in Pozuelo de Alarcon follow a carefully structured academic and personal journey. Early Years Ages 1 to 4 Learn More Primary School Ages 5 to 11 Learn More Secondary School Ages 12 to 16 Learn More Sixth Form Ages 16 to 18 Learn More Bachillerato - BiBac® Ages 16 to 18 Learn More A Levels Ages 16 to 18 Learn More International Baccalaureate Diploma (Candidate School) Ages 16 to 18 Learn More PreviousNext Inspired Education Schools Lead Rankings Across Spain Inspired schools continue to be recognised across Spain’s leading educational rankings, reflecting their commitment to academic excellence, innovation, international outlook and the delivery of a well-rounded education that prepares pupils for success in a global world. Image Image PreviousNext Extraordinary Outcomes We understand that when parents are searching for the best schools in Pozuelo, they want proof, not promises. Through outstanding teaching and personalised support, pupils at The British School of Madrid achieve exceptional academic results in both international and Spanish examinations. IGCSE outcomes consistently surpass UK GCSE averages, while recognition from Universidad Complutense highlights the school’s sustained excellence in EVAU performance over the years. With dedicated, purpose-designed spaces supporting learning and development at every stage, our British school offers an environment where students aged 12 months to 18 years can thrive. Our Early Years facilities have been fully renovated following a significant investment by Inspired Education, creating bright, stimulating spaces tailored for our youngest learners. With 14,000m² of sports facilities, students enjoy an active and healthy lifestyle, with access to football pitches, multi-sport courts, and gyms for each academic stage. Creative expression flourishes in our art studios, high-tech music rooms, and a 1,200m² professional theatre with seating for 300. Together, these spaces form the foundation of a forward-thinking international education, supporting students in realising their potential. Learn More Book a Personalised Tour Take a Virtual Tour Now An Inspired School in Madrid The British School - El Colegio Británico is part of Inspired Education, a leading global group of premium schools. For families, this means students benefit from the expertise, resources, and opportunities of a worldwide network, while still enjoying a school experience rooted in Madrid and connected to the local community. Opportunities include global exchanges, international camps, and collaborations with other schools across the group. Inspired schools are built around 3 pillars: academic excellence, sport, and the performing and creative arts. This balanced approach ensures students develop intellectually, physically, and creatively. At our private school in Pozuelo de Alarcon, Madrid, this philosophy is reflected in daily life through ambitious academic programmes, competitive sport, meaningful performance opportunities, and a strong focus on life skills. Learn More About Inspired Hand-Picked Teachers & Subject Specialists Outstanding teaching begins with deep subject knowledge and exceptional academic preparation. At our international school in Pozuelo, students from the early years through to Sixth Form are taught by highly qualified teachers who are specialists in their fields. Many of our teachers hold degrees from leading universities, including Oxford and other Russell Group institutions. As part of the Inspired Education Group, the school also benefits from a global network of exceptional teaching talent, as well as access to professional development opportunities and world-class academic resources, ensuring our teachers remain at the forefront of educational practice and deliver consistently strong results. Personalised University & Careers Guidance At our private school in Madrid, students receive expert advice on subject selection, university applications, and long-term career planning, helping them approach their next steps with confidence and clarity. With the support of the Inspired Education Group, our university and careers counselling programme provides personalised guidance, helping each student identify their strengths, interests, and future aspirations while securing places at their preferred universities. More than 90% of Inspired graduates gain admission to their first-choice universities worldwide, including leading institutions in the United Kingdom, the United States, Spain, and across Europe. Advanced Technology for Modern Learning The British School of Madrid integrates innovative technology to enhance engagement and support academic success. Classrooms are equipped with modern digital resources designed to personalise learning, including AI-powered platforms that adapt to each student’s pace and learning style. These tools have already delivered strong results across other Inspired schools in Madrid. As part of the Inspired global network, students at our private school in Pozuelo also have access to extensive online resources and opportunities to collaborate with peers at leading schools worldwide. Through virtual exchanges, shared projects, and international competitions, learners connect with students from diverse backgrounds. These experiences simulate real-world multinational workplaces while helping students broaden their horizons and develop valuable life skills. Student Exchange Opportunities Through the Inspired Global Exchange Programme, students at our British school in Madrid can experience life and learning at other outstanding Inspired schools around the world. These exchanges offer unique opportunities to study abroad at prestigious campuses in countries such as the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Belgium, New Zealand, Vietnam, and beyond. Whether participating in a short-term exchange of a few weeks or spending a full academic year overseas, students immerse themselves in new cultures, broaden their perspectives, and build meaningful international friendships. These experiences foster independence, adaptability, and global awareness — qualities that prepare them to thrive in an increasingly interconnected world. International Summer Camps Students at our English school in Pozuelo are invited to participate in Inspired Global Camps, where learning extends far beyond the classroom. These immersive programmes combine sport, creativity, adventure, and academic enrichment, taking place at leading Inspired boarding schools around the world. From improving language skills in the UK to exploring fashion in Milan, surfing in Portugal or taking part in marine adventures in the Bahamas, each camp offers a unique experience. Students return with new skills, lasting friendships, and unforgettable memories that support their personal growth and self-esteem. Hear from Our Students “They gave me everything I needed to study abroad, the support to study in the UK, or in the States or studying here in Spain. It was incredible.” — Victoria, currently studying at Stanford University “It was fundamental, it allowed me to apply in the US, I was on the waiting list at Harvard and Chicago. Having such a broad baccalaureate with so many languages meant you left very well prepared to enter wherever you wanted and to be able to choose where you wanted to go in different countries.” — Ricardo, currently studying at Universidad Complutense “I met teachers here who were really supportive and encouraged me a lot. I was encouraged to be ambitious.” — Isabel, currently studying at Cambridge University PreviousNext Contact Us Today Looking for a top British education in Madrid that opens doors to future opportunities around the world? Get in touch with us and discover how we can help your child become the very best version of themselves. rows.content: Skip to main content Home Areas of practice HR legal advice and employee policies International Employment Law Collective agreements and negotiations with trade unions Litigation and Trials Privacy and Data Security Immigration and Global Mobility Business Restructuring and Business Transfer Occupational Safety and Health Inclusion, Equity and Diversity Training and Specialized Courses Whistleblowing, Compliance, and Investigations Our people News About us Contact Danish (Danmark) You are on our Denmark site See our Global Locations Contact us Home Areas of practice HR legal advice and employee policies International Employment Law Collective Agreements and Negotiations with Trade Unions Litigation and Trials Privacy and Data Security Immigration and Global Mobility Business Restructuring and Business Transfer Occupational Safety and Health Inclusion, Equity and Diversity Training and Specialized Courses Whistleblowing, Compliance, and Investigations Our people News About us About us Careers Privacy policy Contact Danish (Danmark) Immigration and Global Mobility The rules regarding residence and work permits are complicated and undergo frequent changes to accommodate with various political trends. The regulations pertaining to foreign labor in Denmark derive from both EU law and national rules, notably the Danish Aliens Act. Violation of the Danish Aliens Act can result in significant penalties. If an employee does not possess a valid work permit, both the foreign worker and the employer may face fines and imprisonment. It is therefore important for companies to ensure that the relevant residence and work permits are in place and to be attentive to the conditions under which these permits are granted. Work and Residence Permits Different rules apply with regard to obtaining residence and work permits depending on whether the employee is from: Nordic countries (Finland, Iceland, Norway, or Sweden) EU countries (including EEA countries and Switzerland) Third countries (countries not falling under the above categories) Citizens from Nordic countries, the EU, and the EEA can reside and work in Denmark without a work permit. Citizens from Nordic countries must be able to identify themselves if necessary, for example, by presenting a driver's license or other photo identification. Citizens from EU countries, EEA countries, and Switzerland must obtain an EU/EEA residence document if they intend to work in Denmark for more than three months. Citizens from third countries must apply for and obtain both a residence and work permit to work in Denmark. While citizens from third countries may stay in Denmark for a shorter period with a valid visa, they are generally not allowed to engage in work during their stay. Schemes for Residence and Work Permits for Third-Country Nationals Third-country nationals can obtain residence and work permits through various schemes. Below are brief descriptions of some of the most commonly used: Fast-track Scheme The fast-track scheme provides a quick and flexible way for companies to bring foreign labor to Denmark. There are several different types of work permits under the fast-track scheme, each applicable for different purposes. An employer can apply for Danish residence and work permits for the third-country national with a power of attorney from the individual. To use the fast-track scheme, the company must apply for and obtain certification from the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration (SIRI). Income Requirement Scheme The income requirement scheme is for third-country nationals offered a job in Denmark with a high salary. There are no specific educational requirements, and the job does not need to fall within a particular industry. The purpose of the income requirement scheme is to facilitate the entry of highly skilled foreign labor into Denmark. The employee's annual salary must at least meet the income threshold, which is adjusted annually. In 2024, the annual income threshold is DKK 487,000. In 2023, a Supplementary Income Requirement scheme was introduced, setting the income threshold at DKK 393,000 annually (2024 level). According to this scheme, it is a supplementary condition that the position to be filled has been advertised on the Danish recruitment site “Jobnet” and the EURES portal for at least two weeks before a third-country national can apply for residence and work permits for the position. Positive Lists The positive lists are exhaustive lists of various professions facing a shortage of qualified labor in Denmark. These lists are updated every six months based on the needs of the Danish labor market. There is a positive list for individuals with higher education and a positive list for skilled workers. Besides the occupation being on the positive list, several other conditions must be met before this scheme can be used. We are ready to assist if your company requires legal advice in connection to the recruitment and employment of foreign labor. If you need legal advice regarding the above matters, please feel free to contact us for a confidential and non-binding consultation. The need for global mobility within the work force in Denmark these years has never been higher. This has explicitly been said – Denmark needs to attract highly qualified workers. The rules on corporate immigration does however not always meet the intension since there are not just one intension – there is also a need to protect the Danish workforce and avoid social dumping. Therefore, the immigration rules within corporate immigration are not as simply as such and global mobility creates a need for highly qualified counselling, often within different legal areas as well. Holm/Thomsen Law advice you on both the different schemes for work permits, but also on the possible work permit exemption, such as i.a. the fitter rule, exemptions for musicians or artists and professional athletes. Further, we advise you on compliance with the rules and whether a work permit is required, or you can enter on a business visa. Holm/Thomsen Law offers high-quality legal counselling on all aspects of Corporate Immigration Law, i.a.: Work and residence permit for employees and accompanying family member whether it is according to: The fast track scheme, The pay limit scheme, The positive list, or As researcher The fitter rule Business visa Other work permit exemptions EU free movement regulation Read our Q&A section about Corporate Immigration in Denmark Contact us Related services Corporate Immigration Private Immigration Law International Family Law Family Law Global Mobility Wills and Lasting Powers of Attorney Human Rights Holm/Thomsen Law CPHKompagnistræde 16, 3.1208 Copenhagen KDenmarkHolm/Thomsen Law AAR (Virtual Office)Kontorfællesskabet V5B, Vestergade 5B, 1. 8000 Aarhus CDenmark Corporate Immigration in Denmark Corporate Immigration Law International Family Law Private Immigration Law Wills and Lasting Powers of Attorney Family Law in Denmark Family Law Human Rights Legal Notice and Disclaimer Generel Terms & Conditions Privacy Policy +45 21 90 80 06 [email protected] © 2026 Holm/Thomsen Law. rows.content: Skip to content Home Services VAT registration Bringing employees Personal and corporate tax HSE cards/green cards Legal services Company registration Consulting & Legal Accounting People References EN Contact us Payroll Services in Norway – Accurate, Compliant and Efficient Solutions for International Companies Handling payroll in Norway involves more than simply calculating salaries. Norwegian payroll is governed by strict regulations, tax rules, reporting obligations and employee expectations — making it a complex task for international companies operating in the country. At Enter Norway, we offer professional payroll services in Norway designed to simplify your operations, ensure full compliance, and free up time for your core business. Why Payroll in Norway Requires Specialist Knowledge First of all it is mandatory to be a certified accounting firm if you offer legal or accounting services such as work with payroll, VAT, tax, reporting and bookkeeping in Norway. Norwegian payroll systems involve several detailed components with extensive legislation, including: Income tax withholding Employer contributions (social security, pensions) Holiday pay accrual Travel expense reimbursements Sick leave, parental leave and statutory benefits Electronic reporting to Norwegian authorities (A-melding) Payment of net salary, tax, and employer taxes to correct accounts For foreign companies unfamiliar with local requirements, these elements can lead to compliance risks, employee dissatisfaction or costly errors. Providers accounting services for business in Norway who do not have sufficient knowledge about the Norwegian tax, VAT and accounting legislation and do not hold Norwegian certification for offering such services, are operating Illegally. We in Enter Norway Accounting understand that many companies operate under time pressure. That’s why we offer practical, efficient payroll solutions designed to reduce your administrative burden — so you and your team can focus on project delivery. Our Payroll Services – Built for International Operations Enter Norway Accounting delivers full-service payroll solutions in Norway tailored specifically for international and global companies. Whether you’re setting up a branch, executing a project, or expanding operations, we ensure your employees are paid accurately and in accordance with Norwegian legislation. Our payroll services include: Salary calculations and payslip generation Payroll submission to Norwegian authorities Tax and social security withholding and reporting Setup of pension and occupational injury insurance Travel expense and per diem processing Holiday pay calculation and tracking Integration with your accounting systems Ongoing advisory on regulatory changes and best practices We work closely with your HR or project team to ensure every payroll run reflects your company’s structure, employment contracts, and operational needs. We also utilize digital payroll and accounting solutions that ensure secure data flow, system integrations, and efficient reporting – giving you real-time control and transparency. Certified Accounting and Legal Expertise in One Place Enter Norway consists of two dedicated companies – one offering certified accounting services, and one providing legal and consulting expertise – giving you a coordinated, multidisciplinary partner. Our team includes: Accountants with deep knowledge of payroll legislation Legal consultants experienced in employment and contract law Advisors who specialize in cross-border operations As a certified accounting firm, Enter Norway combines payroll services with deep knowledge of Norwegian tax law and business compliance. You can read more about Enter Norway Accounting here. We also assist with: Employment contracts that comply with Norwegian legislation Hiring local employees or posting workers from abroad Social security coordination and A1 documentation Termination handling and final settlements Coordination with HSE card and VAT registration processes Full Outsourcing or Tailored Support – Your Choice We offer flexible payroll solutions depending on your company’s size and needs: Full payroll outsourcing – We manage everything on your behalf Partial support – You handle HR input, we take care of calculations, submissions, and compliance Payroll advisory – Strategic guidance for internal payroll teams needing expert insight Our use of smart accounting and payroll technology allows for efficient data management, accurate reporting, and secure employee communication. Built for Projects, Public Contracts and International Teams Enter Norway has extensive experience supporting some of the world’s largest international companies working on construction projects, public procurement contracts, and technical assignments in Norway. We understand the importance of payroll accuracy for projects with strict deadlines, complex documentation requirements, and multinational staffing. Our clients include both main contractors and subcontractors operating temporarily or long-term in Norway — all of whom benefit from our project-adapted payroll services and coordinated accounting support. More Than Payroll – Integrated Financial and Administrative Services As part of our broader service offering, we also assist with: Accounting and VAT Company registration and compliance HSE cards and employment documentation Import/export support Corporate and personal taxation and assessments Project-based financial advisory In addition, we handle complex services such as reconciliation and control, VAT reporting, annual accounts and cash flow management – With Enter Norway, you get a multidisciplinary partner who supports your entire business in Norway — from employee setup to company closure. The visa routes an immigration lawyer handles in 2026 With the Golden Visa gone, two routes carry most expat moves to Spain: VisaIncome requirement (2026)Work allowed? Non-Lucrative Visa (NLV)€2,400/month passive income for a single applicant (400% of IPREM), plus €600/month per dependantNo: passive income only Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)€2,850/month (200% of the minimum wage, updated January 2026), plus €1,069/month for a spouse and €356/month per childYes: remote work, with at most 20% of income from Spanish clients The DNV also opens the door to the Beckham Law, a flat 24% income tax rate on Spanish-source income up to €600,000 for up to six years. The application (Modelo 149) must be made within six months of the start-of-activity date on your Spanish Social Security registration, and missing that window forfeits it permanently. A lawyer handling your visa will normally bundle the Beckham application into the same instruction. Beyond the headline visas, immigration lawyers in Spain handle family reunification, the arraigo regularisation routes for people already in Spain, work permits, student-visa conversions, visa refusals and appeals, and Spanish nationality applications. Residency paperwork: NIE, TIE and the queues Every route ends in the same paperwork. Your NIE is the identification number Spain uses to track you financially. Nothing of legal significance happens without it. The TIE is the physical residency card non-EU nationals collect once a visa is approved. The bottleneck is appointments. Public NIE and TIE appointment slots in Barcelona and Madrid regularly run 6-8 weeks out; lawyers and gestores have access to appointment channels that aren't available through the public booking system and can often get the same thing done in days. If you're on a deadline (a property completion, a job start date, a visa expiry), that difference is usually the whole reason to instruct someone. The 90-day rule Without a visa, UK and US nationals can spend at most 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen area. Overstaying creates a record that complicates every later application. It's the single most common self-inflicted problem immigration lawyers are asked to fix. What immigration lawyers charge in Spain Immigration and residency work in Spain typically runs €500 to €2,000 as a fixed fee depending on visa type and complexity. A Digital Nomad Visa application with a Beckham Law election sits at the top of that range, a straightforward NLV renewal near the bottom. Get the fee agreement in writing before any work begins; a reputable firm will offer that without being asked. When do you actually need an immigration lawyer? If you're an EU citizen registering residency, or you need a one-off NIE for a bank account, you can usually manage the process yourself. It's form-filling plus patience with the appointment system. A lawyer earns their fee in these situations: Your application has any complication. A previous refusal, an overstay, a criminal-record certificate issue, or income that doesn't fit neatly into the passive/active boxes. These need to be presented correctly the first time. Appeals take months. You're combining a visa with tax planning. The Beckham Law's six-month deadline runs from your Social Security registration in Spain, not from when you get around to it. Visa and tax election need to be sequenced by one adviser. You're on a hard deadline. Professional access to appointment slots is the difference between days and 6-8 weeks in the big cities. Family reunification or nationality. Both are documentation-heavy and unforgiving of gaps; both are routinely refused on technicalities that a specialist would have caught. Not sure which firm fits your situation?Send one enquiry and we’ll route it to the best-fit verified immigration lawyer for your city and case. Free, no obligation. Send an enquiry -> Looking for a different specialty? Property lawyers in Spain · Tax lawyers in Spain · Wills & Inheritance lawyers in Spain · or browse all firms. Frequently Asked Questions How much does an immigration lawyer cost in Spain? Most immigration and residency work is quoted as a fixed fee between €500 and €2,000 depending on the visa and complexity. A Digital Nomad Visa application with a Beckham Law tax election sits at the top of that range. Always get the fee agreement in writing before work begins. Can I still get a Golden Visa in Spain? No. Spain abolished the Golden Visa (residency by €500,000+ property investment) in April 2025. The main routes now are the Non-Lucrative Visa for people with passive income and the Digital Nomad Visa for remote workers. Do the lawyers listed here speak English? Yes. Every firm listed on ExpatLawyerSpain is checked for genuine English-language service before it appears in the directory. That is the point of the site. What if no firm here covers my city? Several listed firms work nationwide and handle immigration matters remotely. Visa applications rarely require you to be in the same city as your lawyer. Send one enquiry and we’ll route it to a firm that covers your situation. We arrange rental accommodation for international talents who have been recruited to work in Sweden by our client companies. A wide range of different properties are sought by our clients, including both apartments and houses in city and suburban locations. Stockholm is the largest market but there is also demand for accommodation in other cities throughout Sweden. There is no charge to property owners/landlords for the service we provide as our client companies pay us to find and arrange suitable accommodation for their relocating staff. We present options to their international talents, based on their requirements and budget. They select the options they are most interested in seeing and we then contact the owners to arrange accompanied viewings. Owners need to be present when viewings take place, usually during the day.Once a rental agreement is reached, we draw up a rental contract and help arrange the property handover. Denmark has more than 6,000 lawyers. Many of them are also legal advisers at the more than 90 local offices (Advokatvagter) which provide free legal advice. If you are arrested and remanded in custody in Denmark, you have the right to have counsel assigned. Please note that the Danish Bar and Law Society does not provide legal advice. Guide: How to Use "Advokatnøglen" The website www.advokatnoeglen.dk contains information about all Danish lawyers. If you are looking for a specific lawyer, you can fill in his/her name and/or firm in the corresponding boxes "navn/firma". If you click on the small map of Denmark, you can search for lawyers in the chosen geographical area. You can also make a geographical search by filling in the postal code, "postnummer", or by choosing the relevant jurisdiction from the drop down menu, "retskreds". To search on the basis of a lawyer’s expressed area of interest, choose the legal topic from the drop down menu, "arbejdsområde". When you select an area of interest, a new drop down menu appears which allows you to specify the legal topic further. In the box "fritekst", you can run a search by typing in your own search terms instead. However, for the moment these categories are available in Danish only. When clicking on "søg", search, you will be provided with the names and contact details of lawyers who satisfy the chosen criteria. However, you lose your right to allowances. As an expert or researcher, it is possible to be allowed to pay a gross tax of 27% of the salary income instead of the regular income tax, for the first seven years (84 months) of employment. In return, one loses any rights to deductions. (Persons liable to tax under the 27% tax scheme must also pay social security contributions amounting to 8%. This means that employees covered by the scheme may have a total minimum tax of 32.84 %). The employer may be Danish or a foreign company or institution with business premises in Denmark, or a foreign company with operations in Denmark. A few general conditions must be fulfilled in order for the rule to apply. The requirements for when the conditions are met may vary depending on whether: One is hired as a researcher with research qualifications, or the job is genuine research work. One is recruited to a specialized or managerial position (key employees) Condition. One must become fully liable to taxation in Denmark at the commencement of employment. If one is hired to do research work, this requirement no longer applies. The scheme may also be utilized by persons of limited tax liability on certain conditions. One may not have had full or limited tax liability in Denmark on salary income or income from businesses for up to 10 years before. Nor may one have been stationed abroad by the employing company. The monthly gross salary must be at least 78.000 DKK (2025). To this must be added labor market contribution and the Danish Labour Market Supplementary Pension or any mandatory foreign social security contributions. The income requirement does not, however, apply to researchers employed to carry out research work, and whose qualifications are accepted by a public research institution or the research councils. One is not permitted to have had a controlling interest in the company through co-ownership for five years prior to employment. Managers can be covered by the scheme, though. We are a listed banking and financial services group with over 180 years of history in Østlandet and head office in Hamar. The bank has contributed to creating value in the market area for several generations. Shortcuts About the SpareBank 1 Alliance News and press releases Subsidiaries Corporate governance Customers dividend Vision and values We are SpareBank 1 Østlandet Local presence SpareBank 1 Østlandet has branch offices across the countys of Innlandet, Akershus, Buskerud and in Oslo. The bank has a physical presence in Norway's most expansive market area and home to around 1.7 million people. We offer our services via local branches, customer service centres and digital surfaces. Our products and services We provide a wide range of financial services to our retail customers, such as financing, savings, money transfer services, insurance, accident prevention, and capital and investment management. Our Corporate Division offers financing for investments and operations, advice, money transfer services in Norway and abroad, interest rate and currency hedging, investment of surplus liquidity, and insurance cover for people and commercial buildings and property. The Corporate Division works closely with the Retail Division and subsidiaries and associated companies that offer leasing, factoring, accounting and advisory services. The division has specialists within insurance, pensions and money transfer services. The Capital Market Division serves high-net-worth individuals and companies, providing good advice and solutions to achieve risk-adjusted returns on free capital. The Bank’s brokerage desk helps to ensure that the needs of import and export companies for foreign currency are met. The Organisation Market Division serves the Norwegian Confederation of Trade Unions (LO) and LO affiliated associations and unions, which are important partners, owners, investors and customers. Listed on Oslo Børs (Stock Exchange) SpareBank 1 Østlandet is an independent bank, which is listed on Oslo Børs. Read more about our equity certificate. The bank is part-owner of SpareBank 1 Gruppen AS (12,4%) and SpareBank 1 Utvikling (18%). Our owners Sparebankstiftelsen Hedmark (the Foundation) is the largest owner. See other large owners here. Our offices Proficient, near and engaged We are here for people and companies to succeed. Together, we contribute to sustainable growth and development in Østlandet. Read more about our business idea, vision and values by clicking the button below. rows.content: top of pageAboutEnglish DepartmentStructureCurriculumTeaching PlansInformationAdmissionsFinancial OverviewContact UsAnti-bullying PolicyDigital LiteracySchool CampsEvents & HolidaysAfter School CareJobsGalleryStaffOm BISDanskafdelingenStrukturÅrsplanerPraktisk-musiske fagInformationerIndskrivningØkonomisk overblikKontakt osUndervisningsmiljøetAntimobbepolitikDigital dannelseLejrskolerLovpligtig dokumentationAktivitets- og ferieplanJobsIntraTeacherIntraStudentIntraParentIntraMoreUse tab to navigate through the menu items.The English DepartmentDiscovery and LearningThe English Department primarily welcomes students from families who reside temporarily in Denmark and expect to continue their education in an international/English-speaking school.* Each class group consists of two-year levels, allowing students to optimise their learning and meet their educational needs. This has proven to be an advantage since we receive students from many different countries with diverse educational experiences. The department consists of 5 classes called A, B, C, D or E. ​ Our Primary classes (A, B, and C) correspond to Years 1-2, 3-4, and 5-6, respectively, following the Cambridge International Primary Programme (CIPP) for Stages 1-6. In the Secondary phase, Class D covers Years 7-8, and Class E includes Years 9-10. Upon successful completion of Year 10, students have the option to advance to Year 11, culminating in the globally recognised Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE). Completing English E with IGCSE qualifications provides an excellent foundation for further studies, enabling students to advance directly to A Levels or the IB Diploma Programme. For Danish high schools (gymnasiums) such as Birkerød or Nørre G, Year 11 (IGCSE) is equivalent to Danish 1g (1st year of High School), Danish 10.klasse, IB MYP5, and pre-IB. International GCSEs and A Levels are studied by over a million students in more than 10,000 schools across 160 countries. Over 1,400 universities worldwide recognise A Level qualifications, including every UK university and 600 in the US, such as all Ivy League institutions. They are also accepted in major student destinations, including Canada, Australia, Singapore, South Africa, Germany, and the Netherlands. At Bjørn's International School, our commitment to a Cambridge education goes beyond academics; it is a strategic preparation for global success. We strive to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary to thrive in an increasingly competitive and dynamic international environment. Danish and English Department Class Structures and Age Groups: ​​​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​​​ * We advise families who intend to settle down in Denmark / extend their stay in the country for a long period of time to enrol their children in the the Danish Department. The Danish Department follows the Danish National curriculum and also offers a diverse and multicultural environment with lessons such as Music, Art, ESL, and Physical Education taught in English. office@bisuv.dk +45 39 29 29 37©2026 by Bjørn's International School. bottom of page

Why choose IES Our Schools Join The Queue Work With Us Our Ethos What we promise to families Since IES was founded in 1993, the three pillars of our ethos have defined life in our schools: Command of English: English is a global language and learning to command both the Swedish and English languages at an early age becomes hugely advantageous later in life. We believe fluency is best achieved through language immersion. Up to half of the education at Internationella Engelska Skolan is delivered through the English language, by native English-speaking teachers. High academic expectations and aspirations: We are convinced that every child can achieve success irrespective of their background. This means we challenge every student to reach their full potential. We are dedicated to supporting students of every background to become responsible citizens and acquire the self-confidence and ambition to do the most with their talents. A safe and calm school environment is a prerequisite for learning: We have clear structures and expectations as this helps students feel secure. This in turn is essential to a good learning environment and signals respect for the value of education. By showing respect for each other and ourselves we lay the foundations for safe and stimulating schooling. Following her breakthrough role as... Award | 27 May 2026 Innovation success for class 6A at IES Lund Students from IES Lund solidified their position as some of the country’s leading young inventors when they received an award in the "Young Innovat... More news "At IES, every student is given the possibility to reach their full potential, regardless of who they are." Linnéa Rudfeldt, Year 9 Frequently Asked Questions and Contact Find the answers to your questions How do I apply to the school? The application window is open all year round, and you can apply to multiple schools at the same time. We admit students on an ongoing basis throughout the year, subject to availability. To apply, please follow these steps: Click on "Apply here". Select the school you wish to apply to (each school has its own queue). You can place your child in the queue from February 1st the year after they were born. Once you click "Apply here", you will be redirected to SchoolSoft’s queue system. Log in using BankID and fill in your personal details. If you do not have a Swedish BankID, you can instead complete the application form available here. I have applied to one school but want to join the queue for a different school instead – what should I do? Each school has their own queue, and it is unfortunately not possible to transfer a queue position or accumulated queue time between schools. However, you are more than welcome to be in the queue for multiple schools simultaneously. You can easily add another school by logging into your SchoolSoft profile. Does it cost anything to attend your school? There are no fees to attend IES schools. Our schools are funded in the same way as those run by the municipality, through the Swedish tax system and the school voucher (skolpeng). Are all your teachers qualified? At IES schools, 85% of teachers are qualified (2024/2025). Roughly 6 out of 10 of these qualified in Sweden, while the remainder have teaching qualifications from abroad, mostly from English-speaking countries. We aim to recruit qualified teachers wherever possible. If we recruit an unqualified teacher, we put a development plan in place to set out how they will become qualified. Swedish school law sets out that where teaching is conducted through the English language, those with a teaching degree from outside of Sweden are also qualified teachers. However, for teachers of English and modern foreign languages, additional requirements must be met to be considered qualified. What would you like to know? Our History Young Swedes should acquire a total inner security when speaking English. Our schools offer the best environment for achieving this. An important part of our success is that we provide a secure environment for teaching and learning. Schools should be a calm environment where teachers can teach and students learn. Principal’s Welcome Principal Nicole MacDonald welcomes you to Futuraskolan International School of Stockholm Work with Us Join a team of internationally minded, dynamic, progressive and enthusiastic staff members Admissions All you need to know about the admission process and how to apply to our school. Futuraskolan International School of Stockholm is a Grade 1-9 independent, non-sectarian, open admissions, co-educational day school located in central Stockholm. The school is designed to serve the children of the international community posted in Sweden and offers all classes in English, with the exception of modern language courses. The school year runs from mid-August to mid-June and has a minimum instructional period of 178 days divided into two semesters. Futuraskolan International School of Stockholm, has a special permit from the Swedish authorities, as it is a school for temporary residents in Sweden and has a set of eligibility requirements. English is the language of instruction and it follows an international curriculum, not the Swedish National Curriculum. For more information on how to apply you are welcome to visit our Admissions page. EAL – We are deeply committed to supporting our EAL learners by providing tailored, differentiated instruction that empowers every student to thrive and succeed from day one. With small push-in and pull-out classes we focus on language development with links to curricular content key words and growing practical and academic vocabulary. Swedish – With a focus on Swedish and connections to the host country, we lift up Swedish so that our learners, no matter where they are from or the length of the time that they are here, feel a connection to this country, the culture, and the Swedish language. Our learners gain proficiency and, in ninth grade if eligible, write the National Test in Swedish with our qualified Swedish teachers. SYV – Our in-house SYV team allows us to focus on high school and our learners, ensuring they receive a place in their English or Swedish school of Choice. We work actively with our learners and parents to help ensure the process is followed and understood. Our results speak for themselves: June 2024 – 1st Choice 79.5%, 2nd Choice – 11.75% Welcome to visit us through our Virtual Tour. With us, your child will learn to thrive in a bilingual environment. Choosing a school for your child is one of the most important decisions you, as a parent, will make. At Internationella Engelska Skolan (IES), our education starts from preschool age. With us, your child will learn to thrive in a bilingual environment. English is gradually introduced through play and song and Swedish is heard all around the school, spoken by staff members and other students. No prior knowledge of English is needed. This creates a solid foundation for a natural development of both Swedish and English. Our students also benefit from a truly international culture, where teachers and fellow classmates hail from many different countries and backgrounds. From preschool age, we lay the groundwork for lifelong learning. Our goal is to provide your child with a calm, safe, and welcoming learning environment, where daily interactions with school leaders, teachers, and other staff are the norm. Through clear goals and expectations, we create the conditions for your child to experience the satisfaction of meeting and exceeding their learning objectives early on. We believe in challenging each student by promoting "grit", the inner motivation to overcome obstacles and reach their full potential. Welcome to Internationella Engelska Skolan. Your choice of school As a parent, you have the right to actively choose where your child will study, whether you opt for a municipal school or an independent school. Popular schools, with more applicants than available places, use different methods to determine which children are offered a place. While municipal schools usually offer places to those who live closest, many independent schools use a queuing system. This means that those who have been in the queue the longest will have the greatest chance of being offered a place at their desired school. At IES, we use this queuing system, and each of our schools has its own queue.
